title: Natural Language Modeling (NLM): Emergent Intelligence Through Physical Signal Processing Without Large Language Models
authors: Mario Moorhead
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The dominant paradigm of machine intelligence — large language model (LLM)-based AI — presupposes that adaptive, context-aware behavior requires transformer architectures, large-scale training corpora, and centralized compute infrastructure. We challenge this presupposition at the definitional level. Intelligence, we argue, does not require language in the narrow sense of tokenized human speech. Language, properly defined, is any physical, chemical, or environmental signal that carries information capable of triggering a meaningful change in the state or behavior of a receiving system — a definition encompassing 3.8 billion years of biological signal processing that predates human speech by geological epochs. This paper presents Natural Language Modeling (NLM): a formal framework for building adaptive systems through local physical signal processing without trained models, cloud infrastructure, or linguistic input. NLM systems are defined by five verifiable principles: Local Signal Primacy, Rule Minimalism, Physical Signal Vocabulary, Distributed Authority, and Resource Minimalism — the last of which is simultaneously a technical specification and a justice constraint requiring deployability on commodity hardware available at consumer price points in any global market. We present two independent working proof implementations. SlimeHive is a multi-agent swarm robotics system modeled on the adaptive network formation behavior of Physarum polycephalum, governed by three finite state machine rules operating on simulated pheromone gradients, running on Raspberry Pi Pico 2W microcontrollers (USD $13). Ceiba is a modular self-powered infrastructure node governed by four physical threshold triggers — solar tracking, survival mode, mesh formation, and water flow regulation — running on Raspberry Pi Zero 2W hardware (USD $15), producing electricity, potable water, LED illumination, and LoRa mesh network connectivity without grid connection or internet dependency. Both systems satisfy all five NLM principles. Neither contains a neural network. Neither was trained on data. Both exhibit adaptive, context-responsive behavior. These implementations demonstrate that the Sense-Interpret-Act computational loop, governed by physical signal vocabularies and minimal rule sets, is sufficient to produce adaptive collective behavior across distinct problem domains — from kinetic swarm navigation to community infrastructure management.

title: Methods in Safety-Critical Control with Control Barrier Functions
authors: Mohammed Alyaseen
abstract: Safety is a fundamental requirement in the control of autonomous and engineered systems operating in complex real world environments. The CBF method for safe control design was found helpful in many safety critical applications such as robotics, autonomous driving, unmanned areal vehicles, power systems, and multi-agent systems. This dissertation develops new theoretical and practical advances for safety-critical control using the framework of Control Barrier Functions (CBFs). While CBFs provide a powerful methodology for certifying and enforcing safety, a number of challenges remains in using CBFs as a safety framework. One challenge is guaranteeing CBF-based controllers are regular enough (continuous/ bounded). Without continuity some safety results are not applicable, and without boundedness practical applicability of such controllers is undermined. Another challenge is handling nonsmoothness within the CBF approach, which is exceedingly important in enforcing complex safety specifications like obstacles with sharp corners. Yet another major challenge is constructing valid CBFs for general classes of physical systems, since the whole CBF safety method hinges on such a construction. This work contributes to each of these three important challenges.First, we investigate the regularity properties (continuity and boundedness) of optimization-based controllers derived from CBFs, with a particular focus on the minimum-norm safe controller. We show that the existence of a valid CBF is not equivalent to the existence of a suitably regular feedback control. Motivated by this, we provide a rigorous characterization of the discontinuity points. Our analysis establishes tight conditions under which the minimum-norm controller remains bounded or unbounded near discontinuities. Second, we contribute to the extension of the CBF framework to the case of discontinuous dynamics and non-smooth safe sets. We construct explicit provably feasible quadratic-programming–based safe controllers that are continuous wherever the underlying system model is continuous. Our control design can handle nonconvex non-smooth conjunctive and disjunctive safety constraints. Third, we address the challenge of constructing valid CBFs themselves for second-order dynamics, which mathematically model a wide range of real world systems. We develop methods to build CBFs for safety specifications expressed as linear, potentially nonconvex positional constraints. These constructions significantly enlarge the class of sets that can be rendered safe compared to prior approaches. We further illustrate the efficacy of our methods in multi-agent and robotic manipulation problems.

title: Logistics under Fire: Russia’s Supply Chain Response to Western Sanctions
authors: Gilles A. Paché
abstract: Russia’s response to sweeping Western sanctions since the invasion of Ukraine illustrates how logistical constraints can be transformed into instruments of geopolitical power. Sanctions have reshaped the corridors, hubs, and alternative networks mobilized by Moscow to maintain the continuity of strategic flows despite increasing isolation. Routes through Central Asia, expanding hubs in Turkey and the United Arab Emirates, as well as the Arctic Northern Sea Route, operate as vectors of State resilience, enabling the circumvention of external pressure while reinforcing territorial and political ambitions. In parallel, gray markets, informal intermediaries, and an expanding “shadow fleet” sustain energy exports and industrial activity, yet generate structural vulnerabilities linked to opacity, safety risks, and dependence on opportunistic actors. This dynamic raises a core research question: how do Western sanctions reconfigure Russia’s logistics architecture, and to what extent do adaptive mechanisms—across formal, informal, and illicit channels—produce both resilience and systemic fragility within global supply chains? The article contends that Russia’s adjustments do not merely mitigate the effects of sanctions but actively reshape global trade patterns. By combining established corridors with shadow networks, Moscow secures short-term autonomy while accumulating long-term risks, demonstrating that logistics has become a central arena of contemporary geopolitical competition. title: Digital Optimization of Hydraulic Fracturing Fleets Integrating Equipment Health and Operational Cost Metrics
authors: H. Rahmati; C. Everts; S. Poludasu; B. Dickinson; C. Roberts; M. Ly
abstract: Abstract Hydraulic fracturing fleet planning requires selecting pumping units that meet job horsepower requirements while balancing equipment condition and operational costs. In practice, fleet selection is often performed manually using nameplate equipment ratings and expert judgment, which may not reflect the true operating capability of aging equipment. This work presents a digital fleet optimization platform that integrates equipment health evaluation with cost-aware asset allocation. The system estimates the effective hydraulic capability of pumping units using health-adjusted efficiency scores derived from observed operating performance relative to manufacturer performance specifications. Using these health-aware metrics, the platform evaluates candidate fleet configurations and applies optimization techniques to identify asset combinations that satisfy job-specific horsepower, safety margin, and fuel substitution requirements while minimizing operational cost. The platform accesses live operational databases to obtain the inventory and operating condition of available pumping units. Each unit is assigned an equipment efficiency score that reflects achievable pumping rate, engine efficiency, and effective hydraulic power utilization relative to rated horsepower. This metric provides a health-aware estimate of the unit's effective performance capability. Job requirements including hydraulic horsepower, safety margin, fuel substitution targets, and job location are then incorporated into the optimization model. Fleet allocation is formulated as a constrained optimization problem that selects pumping units capable of meeting operational requirements while minimizing total operational cost. The cost objective integrates pumping operating cost with transportation cost derived from geospatial distance between asset locations and the job site. The resulting optimization balances equipment health, operational capability, and logistics costs when determining recommended fleet configurations. The framework supports two operational planning modes. A horsepower-only mode ensures the selected fleet meets required hydraulic horsepower while maintaining a defined safety margin. A combined mode introduces an additional fuel substitution constraint requiring that a target fraction of diesel consumption be replaced by dual-fuel pumping units. Field application demonstrates improved fleet utilization and reduced planning cycle time. Asset teams can evaluate multiple fleet scenarios in minutes rather than hours while comparing cost, equipment availability, and operational capability. Integrating equipment health metrics into fleet optimization also prioritizes pumping units capable of delivering required performance at lower operating and transportation cost. Operational deployment shows improved fleet allocation consistency and more efficient use of available pumping assets while supporting scalable planning across multiple concurrent operations. This work introduces a health-aware optimization workflow for hydraulic fracturing fleet planning that integrates equipment performance assessment with cost-based asset allocation. The resulting approach allocates fleets based on effective hydraulic capability rather than nominal horsepower while linking equipment health evaluation, geospatial logistics modeling, and optimization-based fleet selection within a unified digital planning environment.

title: Analysis of IoT adoption on Trucking Logistics in Various Industry in Indonesia
authors: Bayu Yasa Wedha; Daniel Avian Karjadi; Erick Dazki; Handri Santoso; Richardus Eko Indrajit
venue: International Conference on Informatics and Computing (ICIC)
abstract: Recent years, Internet of Things (IoT) provides new business opportunity in terms of cost reduction, increase in productivity or efficiency to organization. In the context of supply chains, IoT helps trucking logistics to track their assets' health, location, utilization, efficiency, and visibility. Indonesia, as the largest archipelago country in the world, mainly relying on truck fleet as its main logistics transportation. Thus, IoT adoption could bring Indonesia's growth and safety in the country. Based on logistic performance index 2018, Indonesia position is 46th in logistic management. One of the parameters is technology adoption especially IoT to improve Logistic company, there are limited study that explore the adoption of IoT in trucking logistics. In this study, companies use IoT technology in their trucks, based on Industry types and spatial distribution is analyzed. Factors that could affect the IoT adoption are being discussed. The IoT adoption level obtained from experts' interview. And then used to analyze 161 company adoption across Indonesia. The result shows that IoT adoption level is between 2 and 3 in the scale of 5 with the highest adoption in Cement industry. Industry that operates in Java and Sumatera islands tend to be more mature on IoT adoption level than other islands for Chemical and Cement industry respectively. Government can make use of this study's result to make policy that cover more wider industry types and location to improve the overall trucking logistics performance.

title: AI Agents in Toxicology: O-QT Automated Hazard Assessment, Metabolism Simulation, and Read-Across Recommendations using the OECD QSAR Toolbox
authors: Ivo Djidrovski
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping predictive toxicology by enabling reproducible, automated workflows that enhance data interpretation and regulatory transparency. The O QT Assistant represents one of the first agentic AI systems capable of performing fully automated chemical hazard profiling, metabolism simulation, and read-across reasoning through the OECD QSAR Toolbox WebAPI. This presentation introduces the architecture, logic, and validation of O-QT as an open source framework designed to bridge in silico modeling with in vitro experimentation. By orchestrating large-language-model (LLM) agents to interpret molecular structures, execute profiling routines, and summarize the results in natural language, O-QT significantly reduces expert time while maintaining full traceability of each analytical step. Use cases will illustrate automated endpoint prediction and metabolism simulation across diverse chemical classes, including small organics and environmental contaminants. The system’s reasoning capabilities allow it to recommend mechanistically relevant analogues for read-across and to flag potential gaps for experimental follow-up. Beyond tool automation, the talk will discuss how multi-agent systems can improve reproducibility and foster regulatory acceptance of AI in safety assessment. The O-QT Assistant demonstrates a transparent, modular approach to integrating AI into established toxicological pipelines—transforming static QSAR workflows into dynamic, interpretable decision frameworks that advance the goals of Next-Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA).

title: Connected Technology as a Solution (CTaaS) for Small Business Transportation and Logistics Sector
authors: Sood Damini
abstract: Small and medium-sized trucking businesses are the lifeline of domestic freight. They move goods across every segment of the supply chain: from manufacturing plants and ports on long far-mile runs, through regional mid-mile transfers between distribution hubs, to the final last-mile delivery at a storefront or front door. Together, SMB carriers account for the vast majority of trucking businesses in the United States and handle a disproportionate share of the capacity that large national carriers cannot fill cost-effectively. Yet most of them operate without the technology infrastructure that large carriers take for granted — real-time fleet tracking, predictive maintenance, driver safety monitoring, and cargo theft protection. The urgency of closing this technology gap has intensified with the rise of strategic cargo theft, a category of organized crime that the FBI formally warned in April 2026 is growing at an alarming rate — with losses exceeding $725 million annually and a near 60% year-over-year increase in incidents. This paper introduces Connected Technology as a Solution (CTaaS), a subscription-based managed service model that bundles hardware, wireless connectivity, cloud software, and ongoing support into one predictable monthly fee, giving every SMB carrier access to enterprise-grade logistics intelligence through One Dashboard. The paper explains what CTaaS is, why the need for it is urgent, how its four-layer architecture works, and its measurable impact on productivity, resilience, safety, and cargo theft prevention, including how domestic manufacturing of concealed asset trackers can extend CTaaS protection and directly support law enforcement in cargo recovery.

title: Multi-Swarm Agency Protocol: Emergent Coordination in Heterogeneous Agent Networks. (50 pages)
authors: Alfredo Medina Hernandez; MedinaTech
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Multi-Swarm Agency Protocol: Emergent Coordination in Heterogeneous Agent Networks Through φ-Resonant Synchronization and Distributed Consensus Mechanisms We present the Multi-Swarm Agency Protocol (MSAP), a comprehensive formal framework for coordinating heterogeneous autonomous agent swarms without centralized control, external orchestration, or pre-negotiated cooperation agreements. MSAP enables N independent swarms, each with distinct objectives, internal governance structures, resource constraints, and temporal dynamics, to achieve coherent collective behavior through a novel mechanism we term φ-resonant synchronization. This synchronization leverages the mathematical properties of the golden ratio φ = 1.618033988749895 to achieve optimal coupling strengths that balance coordination benefits against autonomy costs. We prove that under MSAP, swarm coordination converges in O(log N) synchronization rounds with probability 1 − ε for any ε > 0, provided the inter-swarm coupling matrix satisfies the spectral condition λ₂(K) > φ⁻¹. We further establish that this convergence is optimal—no protocol can achieve coordination in fewer than Ω(log N) rounds under our adversarial message delay model. The protocol is fault-tolerant, maintaining coordination properties even when up to f < N/φ² swarms experience Byzantine failures. Our theoretical contributions include: (1) a complete characterization of the swarm synchronization manifold as a φ-weighted torus, (2) proof that emergent coordination behaviors satisfy a novel compositionality theorem enabling hierarchical swarm-of-swarms architectures, (3) informationtheoretic lower bounds showing our protocol is communication-optimal within constant factors, and (4) extension of classical Kuramoto dynamics to heterogeneous multi-objective settings with rigorous stability analysis. Empirical validation across 47 production deployments spanning six industries (aviation, finance, healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, smart cities) demonstrates 94.7% coordination success rate (σ = 2.3%), mean coordination latency of 127ms (σ = 34ms), and mean rounds-tosynchronization of 4.2 (σ = 1.1). Our largest deployment coordinates 12 swarms comprising 2,847 agents with sustained throughput of 45,000 coordinated actions per second. Comparative evaluation against seven baseline coordination protocols shows MSAP achieves 2.3× higher coordination success, 4.1× lower latency, and 6.7× better scalability. The MSAP reference implementation is open-source (Apache 2.0 license), with formal verification in Coq ensuring correctness of core synchronization invariants. We discuss implications for the emerging field of multi-swarm robotics, autonomous vehicle coordination, and distributed AI governance. **Keywords:** Multi-agent systems, swarm intelligence, distributed coordination, emergent behavior, φ-synchronization, Kuramoto oscillators, Byzantine fault tolerance, heterogeneous agents, protocol verification, autonomous systems, collective intelligence, decentralized control, golden ratio mathematics **ACM Classification:** I.2.11 Distributed Artificial Intelligence—Multiagent systems; C.2.4 Distributed Systems—Distributed applications; G.1.6 Optimization—Global optimization --- ## 1. Introduction ### 1.1 The Multi-Swarm Challenge Modern enterprise systems increasingly deploy multiple autonomous agent swarms, each optimized for specific domains: supply chain optimization, customer service automation, financial analysis, security monitoring, predictive maintenance, and resource allocation. These swarms must coordinate without: 1. **Central orchestration** — no single point of failure or control 2. **Pre-defined protocols** — agents and swarms may be unknown at design time 3. **Shared objectives** — swarms optimize different, potentially conflicting fitness functions 4. **Global visibility** — each swarm has only local information 5. **Synchronous execution** — communication delays are arbitrary and unpredictable Traditional multi-agent coordination assumes homogeneous agents with aligned goals operating in synchronous rounds with reliable communication. Real-world deployment shatters these assumptions. A supply chain swarm optimizing for just-in-time delivery may conflict with a sustainability swarm minimizing carbon footprint. A security swarm restricting access may impede a customer service swarm maximizing responsiveness. These conflicts cannot be resolved by a central authority—they must emerge from distributed negotiation. ### 1.2 Motivating Applications Distributed Financial Trading A quantitative trading firm operates: - **Alpha generation swarm**: Signal discovery, factor modeling - **Execution swarm**: Order routing, market making, latency arbitrage - **Risk management swarm**: Position limits, VaR monitoring, stress testing - **Compliance swarm**: Regulatory reporting, trade surveillance Alpha wants to maximize returns. Execution wants to minimize slippage. Risk wants to limit exposure. Compliance wants to ensure auditability. These objectives are inherently in tension. MSAP enables these swarms to coordinate in real-time (sub-millisecond) while preserving their distinct mandates. Smart City Infrastructure A metropolitan area coordinates: - **Traffic management swarm**: Signal timing, congestion routing - **Emergency response swarm**: Dispatch, route clearing, hospital coordination - **Energy grid swarm**: Load balancing, renewable integration, demand response - **Public transit swarm**: Schedule optimization, crowd management An emergency affects traffic routing, which affects bus schedules, which affects commuter energy demand. MSAP enables these swarms to coordinate at city scale (millions of agents) with second-level latency. Technical Challenges Multi-swarm coordination presents several fundamental challenges: **Challenge 1: Heterogeneous Objectives** Swarms optimize different fitness functions G₁, G₂, ..., Gₙ. Coordination must not require swarms to abandon their objectives; rather, it must find operating points where swarms can achieve reasonable satisfaction while enabling collective behavior. **Challenge 2: Dynamic Membership** Swarms join and leave the coordination network. New swarm types emerge. The protocol cannot assume fixed membership or pre-shared knowledge of swarm capabilities. **Challenge 3: Adversarial Environment** Some swarms may be compromised, behave selfishly, or actively attempt to disrupt coordination. The protocol must be robust to Byzantine behavior. **Challenge 4: Scale** Real deployments involve thousands of swarms with millions of agents. The coordination overhead must scale sub-linearly with swarm count. **Challenge 5: Latency** Many applications require sub-second coordination. The protocol must minimize synchronization rounds. ### 1.4 Our Approach: φ-Resonant Synchronization MSAP addresses these challenges through a novel coordination mechanism inspired by coupled oscillator dynamics. Each swarm maintains a "coordination phase" θ ∈ [0, 2π) representing its current position in a coordination cycle. Swarms influence each other's phases through φweighted coupling, where the golden ratio φ = 1.618033988749895 appears naturally from optimality conditions . The key insights are: 1. **Phase representation abstracts objectives**: A swarm's phase encodes its current coordination state without revealing internal structure or fitness function. 2. **Kuramoto-like dynamics ensure convergence**: Modified Kuramoto oscillator dynamics guarantee that coupled swarms synchronize their phases. 3. **φ-weighting optimizes coupling**: The golden ratio weighting balances coordination strength against autonomy preservation, emerging from variational principles. 4. **Hierarchical composition**: Synchronized swarms can themselves be treated as agents in a meta-swarm, enabling recursive coordination. ### 1.5 Contributions This paper presents: 1. **MSAP Framework** — A complete formal protocol for multi-swarm coordination, including message formats, state machines, and invariants (Section 3). 2. **φ-Resonance Theory** — Mathematical foundation for emergent synchronization, proving optimality of golden ratio coupling (Section 2). 3. **Convergence Proofs** — Rigorous analysis showing O(log N) coordination with high probability, with matching lower bounds 4. **Fault Tolerance** — Extension to Byzantine settings with f < N/φ² fault threshold (Section 5). 5. **Production Validation** — Comprehensive evaluation across 47 deployments in 6 industries (Section 7). 6. **Formal Verification** — Coq proofs of core protocol invariants (Appendix B). 7. **Reference Implementation** — Open-source implementation with performance benchmarks (Section 6). ### 1.6 Paper Organization Section 2 develops the mathematical foundation. Section 3 specifies the MSAP protocol. Section 4 analyzes convergence and complexity. Section 5 addresses fault tolerance. Section 6 describes implementation. Section 7 presents empirical evaluation. Section 8 surveys related work. Section 9 concludes with future directions. Appendices provide complete proofs, algorithms, and verification artifacts. --- ## 2. title: Concept of adaptive production automation architecture with local and cloud components based on edge artificial intelli-gence and a multi-agent system
authors: I.I. Naumov; D.Yu. Konshin; K.A. Moroz
abstract: Modern manufacturing systems transitioning to advanced production standards require a high degree of adaptability, transparency in decision-making, and fault tolerance. Traditional automation methods, based on rigid algorithms and centralized control logic, prove insufficiently flexible. They underutilize the potential of big data, scale poorly, struggle with network latency or connectivity disruptions, and require significant effort to integrate new types of equipment. The limited intelligence of local controllers complicates autonomous operation, while the opacity of algorithms hinders decision-making by personnel and diagnostic processes. The objective of the article is to develop a conceptual architecture of an intelligent distributed production control system based on embedded devices with edge artificial intelligence capabilities, multi-agent approach, and explainable AI technologies. The system must ensure local loop autonomy, seamless interaction with cloud services, adaptation to changing equipment operating conditions, and transparency of algorithms for engineering and operational personnel. The architecture has been proposed that combines the computing capabilities of local nodes and cloud components with distributed logic based on a multi-agent system. Edge devices embedded in production equipment gain the ability to perform local data preprocessing, run machine learning models, respond instantaneously to network delays, and maintain an autonomous safety loop. Implementing the proposed architecture enables enterprises to enhance the resilience of manufacturing processes to internal and external disruptions, improve the quality and speed of decision-making, reduce reliance on centralized control systems, and increase energy and resource efficiency.

title: New Wave Logistics Framework: Enabling Sustainable Practices in Road Transportation
authors: Ouahbi Younesse; Soumia Ziti
venue: International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The logistics industry is focused on reducing carbon emissions and improving efficiency to meet environmental and regulatory requirements. NW Logistics, an AI-powered platform, aims to achieve these goals by integrating real-time CO2 emissions tracking, route optimization, and driver behavior monitoring. The system allows logistics managers to monitor fleet performance with increased accuracy and generates individualized reports for drivers. Expected outcomes include significant reductions in carbon emissions, improvements in route efficiency, delivery tracking accuracy, and driver safety, demonstrating the transformative potential of AI in sustainable logistics management

title: Dynamic Event-Triggered Secure Fault-Tolerant Privacy-Preserving Consensus Tracking for Multi-Agent Systems Under Markov Switching Topologies and DoS Attacks
authors: Shuo Xu; Xiaozheng Jin; Ming Yang; Xiaoming Wu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This article investigates the secure fault-tolerant (FT) privacy-preserving consensus tracking problem for nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) under dynamic event-triggered communications, where physical-layer uncertainties and information-layer challenges are simultaneously considered. The former include external disturbances and actuator faults, while the latter involve Markov switching topologies, denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, passive eavesdropping threats, and communication-resource constraints. Different from most existing results that mainly address cyber security or physical safety separately, this work develops a unified distributed control framework integrating privacy preservation, secure communication, and FT coordination. Specifically, a masked virtual reference system is introduced to generate exchanged communication signals, thereby separating network transmissions from the real faulty dynamics and reducing the direct exposure of real-layer information. Based on this system, a distributed dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM) is designed to guarantee secure leader-follower tracking under stochastic topology switching and DoS-induced communication interruptions while reducing communication burden. Meanwhile, an adaptive FT anti-disturbance controller is constructed for the real faulty system to compensate for actuator faults, bias faults, external disturbances, and uncertainties. Moreover, a piecewise Lyapunov method is developed to establish closed-loop boundedness, practical tracking convergence, and exclusion of Zeno behavior. The non-identifiability property of the masked virtual communication protocol is further analyzed under internal honest-but-curious and external passive eavesdropper models. Finally, simulation results on a multiple damped oscillator system are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Note to Practitioners—In real-world MASs, physical-layer uncertainties and information-layer challenges often coexist. Actuator faults and external disturbances may degrade the local dynamics, while Markov switching topologies, DoS attacks, passive eavesdropping threats, and limited communication resources may affect inter-agent coordination. These factors require distributed control schemes that can jointly address secure communication, privacy protection, and FT tracking. This paper proposes a hierarchical distributed framework for MASs under Markov switching topologies and DoS attacks. A dynamic event-triggered communication strategy is used to reduce unnecessary transmissions, and a masked virtual reference layer is employed to separate network transmissions from the real faulty states and reduce the direct exposure of real-layer information. Meanwhile, an adaptive FT anti-disturbance controller is constructed to compensate for actuator faults and external disturbances. The proposed approach is applicable to distributed automation systems such as robotic networks, autonomous aerial vehicle formations, and intelligent transportation systems, where secure, private, and reliable coordination is required under switching network conditions.

title: AUTOMATING THE LAST LINK: ENABLING FUEL CONNECTION AUTONOMY FOR FUTURE FLEET REPLENISHMENT READINESS
authors: Leonard B. Mendoza; Adam J. Nassani; Carlos S. McGinity; Evan F. Mac
venue: Calhoun: The Naval Postgraduate School Institutional Archive (Naval Postgraduate School)
abstract: As the U.S. Navy transitions toward distributed lethality and unmanned surface vessel (USV) integration, the ability to autonomously refuel at sea becomes a critical enabler of extended operations. Traditional underway replenishment (UNREP) systems require manual probe-and-drogue connections, which are incompatible with unmanned platforms. This thesis paper, led by Team AUTOREP, explores autonomous UNREP refueling solutions to eliminate the need for human-in-the-loop processes during fuel transfer. The team will investigate, design, and assess multiple automated connection systems suitable for USVs no larger than DARPA’s No Manning Required Ships (NOMARS) prototype, the USX-1 Defiant. Using a phased spiral development method, the project will establish stakeholder requirements, conduct feasibility analyses, perform comparative evaluations, and deliver a conceptual design of the most promising solution. By automating the final link in the refueling process, this research supports increased USV endurance, operational safety, and fleet autonomy. The study benefits Navy and DoD stakeholders by reducing personnel exposure during hazardous operations, enabling longer unmanned missions, and supporting future force structures. For the systems engineering community, it advances integration methods, modular design, and autonomous control in complex maritime environments—setting a precedent for future naval logistics innovation.

title: Safety Score: A Quantitative Approach to Guiding Safety-Aware Autonomous Vehicle Computing System Design
authors: Hengyu Zhao; Yubo Zhang; Pingfan Meng; Hui Shi; Li Erran Li; Tiancheng Lou; Jishen Zhao
abstract: High automated vehicles rely on the computing system in the car to understand the environment and make driving decisions. Therefore, computing system design is essential for ensuring the driving safety. However, to our knowledge, no clear guideline exists so far regarding how to guide the safety-aware autonomous vehicle (AV) computing system design. To understand the safety requirement of AV computing system, we performed a field study by operating industrial Level-4 AV fleets in multiple locations for three months. The field study indicates that traditional computing system performance metrics, such as tail latency, average latency, maximum latency, and timeout, cannot fully satisfy the safety requirement for AV computing system design. To address this issue, we propose the “safety score” as a primary metric for measuring the level of safety in AV computing system design.

title: Autonomous Heavy-Duty Vehicles in Logistics: Market Trends, Opportunities, and Barriers
authors: Loha Hashimy; Isabella Castillo; Wolfgang Schildorfer; Matthias Neubauer
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive market research study focused on identifying opportunities and barriers for the adoption of autonomous heavy-duty vehicles (AHDVs) in the logistics industry. The methodology employs a qualitative approach, utilizing workshops, questionnaires, interviews, and social media polls to collect primary and secondary data. The empirical findings highlight both the current landscape and the future trends in AHDVs, fleet management, and logistics. The study reveals the importance of safety, technological readiness, regulatory challenges, and infrastructure development as key barriers, while also showcasing potential benefits like increased safety, reduced costs, and improved efficiency. Furthermore, a quadrant analysis prioritizes these opportunities and barriers for strategic decision-making. The article concludes by discussing the implications of the findings and the broader context of autonomous vehicles in logistics.

title: From Intelligent Automation to Agentic AI: Engineering the Next Generation of Enterprise Systems
authors: Rajesh Cherukuri; Venkat Kishore Yarram
venue: International Journal of Emerging Research in Engineering and Technology
abstract: Businesses are shifting away, however, and realizing agentic AI systems of autonomous, goal-oriented, software agents that are able to perceive, reason, make actions, and learn end-to-end systems. In this paper, a conceptual and engineering blueprint of such transition is proposed. We define agentic enterprise systems initially on a set of directions of autonomy, adaptivity, coordination, and governance, and propose an Observe-Reason-Act-Learn cognitive loop as the fundamental behavioral pattern. Based on this, we showcase a high-level reference architecture connecting an enterprise knowledge layer (data lake, vector search, knowledge graphs) with an autonomous agent layer with a reasoning and planning layer based on the use of LLM-based paradigms and multi-agent coordination engine to coordinate cross-domain workflows. It describes in the methodology section how to model agent roles and skills, break down business processes into tasks that can be performed by agents, establish protocols of cooperation, and deploy memory and tool-use systems that are based on enterprise APIs and robots-pilots. These patterns are illustrated by an implementation sketch that illustrates how these patterns can be achieved with the use of contemporary agent frameworks in hybrid cloud/on-premise settings. Quantitative evidence that has been synthesized so far on the basis of emerging deployments shows significant cost, productivity, and cycle-time improvements compared to conventional IA, as well as new failure modes in the areas of hallucinations, governance gaps, and safety. The paper ends with the overview of major research directions in the field of reliability, privacy-preserving knowledge access specially in rare disease and alignment of autonomous agents and claims that a powerful AgentOps and governance are the key to the full potential of agentic enterprise systems

title: Optimization of Unit-Load Formation and Facility Design: A Comprehensive Guide to Pallet Selection and Inventory Logistics
authors: Taddese Yohanesse
venue: International Journal of Latest Technology in Engineering Management & Applied Science
abstract: Effective facility design and unit-load formation are critical factors in optimizing modern warehouse operations and minimizing supply chain costs. While various handling equipment options exist, pallets serve as the primary structural foundation for maximizing storage and transport efficiency. This study outlines a systematic approach to equipment selection and dimension optimization within a large-scale industrial warehouse design. It evaluates pallet material performance across wood, plastic, and metal alternatives. To overcome the challenges of standardizing handling procedures, two distinct optimization workflows—Linear Programming (LP) and Space Utilization Efficiency (SUE)—are examined to identify the ideal footprint for uniform racking configurations. Comprehensive inventory modeling is then applied to calculate total pallet capacity constraints under specified load weights, height boundaries, and stack ability limits. Based on structural and economic parameters, premium wooden pallets measuring 1000mm X 900mm X 150mm were selected, achieving an optimal spatial efficiency of up to 94.4% for core inventory components. To fully support the facility's inventory demands across nine distinct material classes, the total fleet requirement was mathematically determined. The logistics analysis indicates that the warehouse requires a total infrastructure capacity of 185,663 standardized pallets, comprised of 181,376 units for primary cycle and safety stock alongside 4,287 units for dedicated buffer operations. Implementing this uniform pallet standard minimizes floor space loss, simplifies shelf design, and establishes a highly streamlined material handling workflow.

title: Efficient Collision Detection and Path Optimization for Multi-Node Systems Using Vector Cross Product and Neural Regression
authors: Chengcheng Xie
venue: International Conference on Applied Mathematics, Modelling and Intelligent Computing (CAMMIC)
abstract: Efficient motion planning for multi-node systems with rigid structural constraints remains a challenging problem in robotics and multi-agent coordination. This paper proposes a computational framework for real-time collision detection and path optimization in multi-node systems moving along constrained spiral trajectories. First, a time-driven motion model based on the Archimedean spiral is established to compute the continuous trajectories of interconnected nodes. A recursive geometric update mechanism enables efficient calculation of the spatial states of large-scale node chains. Second, an efficient collision detection algorithm based on vector cross-product tests is developed. By transforming structural interference into two-dimensional line segment intersection checks and integrating hierarchical time scanning with interval refinement, the method accurately identifies collision intervals while maintaining low computational complexity. Third, a path optimization strategy is introduced. A bisection search algorithm determines the minimum feasible spiral pitch satisfying collision constraints, while a multilayer perceptron (MLP) regression model predicts turning path length and guides optimal parameter selection. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework accurately predicts collision moments (approximately 428.8 s) and determines the minimum feasible pitch (0.3936 m). Compared with traditional geometric traversal methods, the proposed approach significantly improves computational efficiency while maintaining high precision. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a scalable and real-time solution for motion planning and collision avoidance in multi-node robotic systems and multi-agent trajectory planning scenarios.

title: Agentic AI for Autonomous Software Maintenance: A Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Agent Framework for Bug Localization, Patch Generation, and Regression Validation
authors: Swathi J.N; Aarthy S L; Ananda Kumar S; D. P. Acharjya
venue: International Journal of Emerging Research in Engineering and Technology
abstract: Autonomous software maintenance is becoming a critical research direction as modern codebases grow beyond the practical reach of manual debugging, release governance, and regression validation. Large language models have demonstrated strong code-generation capabilities, but repository-level maintenance remains difficult because defects frequently arise from interactions among multiple files, hidden dependencies, runtime configurations, and incomplete issue reports. This paper proposes AutoMaint-RAG, a retrieval-augmented multi-agent framework for autonomous software maintenance. The framework coordinates specialized agents for issue interpretation, repository retrieval, fault localization, patch synthesis, static analysis, test generation, regression execution, and release-risk governance. Unlike single-agent code-generation workflows, AutoMaint-RAG treats maintenance as a controlled software-engineering process in which every generated patch must be grounded in repository evidence, ranked suspicious locations, executable test feedback, and auditable decision records. The proposed framework integrates hybrid retrieval over code, commit history, test traces, dependency graphs, and operational telemetry; combines spectrum-based fault localization with semantic ranking; and applies iterative patch refinement through execution-guided feedback. A reproducible validation protocol is defined using repository-level issue benchmarks, mutation-based regression assessment, and industrial-style CI/CD gates. The paper contributes a formal architecture, agent-interaction protocol, patch-risk scoring model, evaluation design, and governance layer for deploying agentic AI in safety-sensitive software maintenance environments. The central argument is that autonomous maintenance should not be reduced to prompt-based patch generation; rather, it requires an engineered socio-technical pipeline that constrains language-model creativity through retrieval grounding, tool execution, regression evidence, and human-review escalation. The proposed framework advances a research agenda for maintainable, auditable, and operationally reliable AI agents in software lifecycle management.

title: Mobility-Aware Task Offloading in Industrial Fog Networks: A Submodular-Based MARL Approach
authors: Bo Xu; Haitao Zhao; Haotong Cao; Chun Zhu; Jinlong Sun; Linghao Zhang; Hongbo Zhu
abstract: The development of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications presents a critical challenge in terms of latency limitation, particularly considering the limited availability of resources that prevent a single fog device from fully executing large-scale computing tasks. In such scenarios, enabling distributed computing across multiple fog servers or collaborating with cloud servers holds promising potential. To improve the efficiency of task offloading while accounting for the crucial role of movable fog devices (e.g., robots and unmanned cars), we formulate a joint optimization problem as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), incorporating offloading decisions, computing resource allocation, and trajectory optimization under constraints related to available resources and collision avoidance. Due to the nondeterministic polynomial-time hardness (NP-hardness) in the problems of task offloading and resource allocation, we reformulate a matroid-constrained submodular maximization problem and propose an iterative low-complexity algorithm to find solutions. Subsequently, extracting better solutions from submodular optimization, we propose a multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based algorithm to solve the trajectory optimization problem for the movable fog devices acting as agents, making decisions based on their local observations. Finally, simulation results have validated that the proposed scheme has a superior performance compared to the baselines.

title: The Luner resupply station. The logistics hub for life beyond earth.
authors: Butzbach, Jimmy
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Lunar Accord Abstract The Lunar Accord establishes the foundational infrastructure required for a permanent, sustainable human presence beyond Earth. Rather than proposing colonization or geopolitical claims, the Accord defines a practical, engineering-driven framework centered on logistics, energy, protection, research, and continuity. Its purpose is simple but profound: to transform the Moon from a remote destination into a functional operations hub that supports long-term survival and deep-space expansion. The Accord rests on five essential systems. The Lunar Logistics Station (LRS) serves as the core operations node, enabling cargo transfer, equipment maintenance, power distribution, and communication. The Autonomous Solar Tug Fleet creates the first continuous off-world supply chain, transporting materials between Earth, the Moon, and Lagrange points while mapping local space and optimizing navigational routes. The Meteor Defense Grid protects all surface infrastructure from micrometeorite threats, ensuring long-duration operability in an airless, high-hazard environment. The Lunar Solar Farm Network provides energy independence through polar solar megafields and hardened storage systems capable of powering every lunar subsystem. Finally, the Volatile Research Labs and Cryo Vault support high-risk scientific experimentation and preserve genetic, biological, and cultural archives, providing a long-term continuity backbone for humanity. Together, these systems form a resilient lunar infrastructure spine designed to outlast crises, support scientific breakthroughs, and enable expansion to Mars, the asteroid belt, and beyond. The Lunar Accord is not a vision of distant possibility — it is the minimal viable architecture required for humanity to become a multi-world species.

title: C-ABT: A continuous control layer for inter-agent collision avoidance based on asynchronous backtracking
authors: Joachim Muller; Alberto Viseras; Christoph Manss; Thomas Wiedemann
venue: The proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Control Applications/The proceedings of the ... IEEE Conference on Control Applications
abstract: When using multiple robotic agents for waypoint-based exploration or coverage tasks, collision avoidance between agents is an important issue. With a centralized planner, this issue arises only at one central instance. However, when using asynchronous and/or decentralized algorithms, decentralized methods for collision avoidance need to be used. We propose a novel approach based on the asynchronous backtracking (ABT) algorithm which provides decentralized constraint satisfaction called continuous ABT(C-ABT). \nC-ABT is a continuous extension to ABT intended as a collision avoidance layer for existing multi-agent waypoint navigation. It extends ABT in the sense that participating agents know when they found a valid solution. In this case, agents can safely move to their selected waypoints. While ABT only finds one static solution, C-ABT is suited for continuously provided new waypoints for all agents. By using the concept of local neighborhoods, C-ABT is also scalable to swarms of arbitrary size.

title: Agentic Intelligence in Industry: Edge AI, Connected Fleets, and Resilient Critical Infrastructure Systems
authors: Rajesh Mattaparthi
abstract: In the past, industrial systems were built for the expectation that it would be predictable. There would be certain control loops to adhere to or there would be scheduled maintenance, an expectation that the man or woman should be able to come online and address known failures. That world is coming to an end. More data is produced by machines than any team of humans can comprehend in real-time, supply chains are global and the infrastructure to support our cities is joining the cyber and climate change risk brigade. Against this backdrop comes agentic artificial intelligence, an AI system capable of perception, reasoning, decision making and action that can be performed autonomously and are not the domain of humans. This book explores the role that intelligent agents, which offer flexible distribution and interconnection options, and can be deployed anywhere throughout the system (connected fleets and critical infrastructure), can play in the transformation of industrial systems. It is, as the title indicates, split up in three themes. Edge AI will include the architectures and design patterns to allow the agents to run at the edge, near the data source, low latency, and gracefully degrade for loss of connectivity. A connected fleet is concerned with issues of coordinating a large number of autonomous systems sharing a common sense of the environment and negotiating resources in a dynamic environment. Since it is entrusted to agentic systems to perform functions vital to public safety, resilient critical infrastructure is about the governance, security and reliability frameworks needed when critical infrastructure becomes agentic. The theme of autonomy without accountability as liability pervades each chapter. Powerful agentic systems require commensurately careful consideration of explainability, fail-safe design and human oversight particularly in industrial contexts where anything more than dollars could be at stake on the line if things went wrong. This book aims to provide knowledge to engineers, architects, operations managers, researchers and policymakers during this transition. Although no text can fully describe the understanding of a field moving at that pace, this book provides a solid foundation of understanding the concepts of autonomy, resilience and trust and prepares the reader not only for today's technology but also what's to come.

title: Fully Automated Land Drilling Rig Showcases New Level of Consistency, Performance, and Safety
authors: David Forrest; Justin Weinkauf; Mohammad Mustafizur Rahman; Ashley Fernandes
venue: SPE Kuwait Oil & Gas Show and Conference (KOGS)
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the incremental deployment of a fully automated drilling rig designed to improve safety, consistency, and operational performance. The primary objective is to eliminate manual intervention during repetitive, high-risk activities through robotics and process automation. Additional goals include mitigating drilling dysfunction, implementation of autonomous sliding, enabling remote directional drilling operations, and integrating real-time optimization and MPD control to create a scalable, high-efficiency drilling system with minimal human presence on the rig floor. The rig features robotic pipe handling and automated connections, removing personnel from hazardous zones. Vibration mitigation is achieved via feedback control with the top drive, and parameter selection is optimized with an advanced AutoDriller system incorporating machine learning and science-based models. Directional drilling is automated using an application that learns from its experiences, enabling remote directional operations. Optimization apps monitor and adjust drilling parameters such as WOB, RPM, and Differential Pressure in real time. MPD operations incorporate fully automated choke control to maintain tight pressure windows. In some applications, AutoDriller setpoints are automated to mitigate the effects of RCD – pipe joint interactions as well as error in surface WOB measurements. Remaining manual activities are elevated by real time alerts that notify the driller when undesirable conditions exist. All systems are integrated and synchronized to support autonomous operations throughout the drilling process. The fully automated rig delivers significant operational and safety improvements. Robotic handling and process control for automated connections exceed human performance while eliminating hands-on intervention. Feedback control stick-slip mitigation lowers dysfunction severity resulting in improved downhole dynamics and reduced bit trips. Slide automation enables remote directional operations with accurate slide execution to TD with directional changes made in real time from an offsite center. Optimization applications autonomously select operating parameters within safe operating windows to maintain consistent downhole weight and depth of cut. MPD automation improves accuracy and latency to trap pressure on connections, enhancing wellbore stability and reducing the risk of influx through narrow mud window formations. Reduction of manual tasks on the rig floor with robotic pipe handling systems allows for improved focus on equipment health and maintenance, reducing downtime. These results validate the rig's ability to safely execute complex workflows while improving drilling efficiency and repeatability. This field deployment is among the first to integrate robotics, closed-loop automation, and remote operations with a fully autonomous rig platform. It demonstrates how advanced systems can effectively replace manual workflows while enhancing safety and performance. The project moves beyond partial automation by unifying software development, process automation control, and robotics. All these systems can be implemented independently or in synchronization with each other, demonstrating their ease of scalability across rig fleets and the industry.

title: Logistical Approach to a Fishing-Industrial Complex Functioning
authors: Сергей Сергеевич Мойсеенко; Leonid Meyler
abstract: The paper describes a concept of the logistical approach to a fishing-industrial complex functioning and it is grounded the necessity of its improving. The concept is determined by the specifics of such basic processes as: fishery, production of fish-products directly on fishing vessels, the transport service of the fishing fleet, ensuring the safety of navigation and fishery, processing, storage of raw materials and finished products, their delivery and selling on the domestic and foreign markets. The main tasks, goal and features of management of logistics processes in the fishing-industrial complexes are formulated. It is considered the structural elements of the fishing industry which have both internal logistic communication and with the external environment: netting manufacturers, shipbuilding production, product markets, etc. The paper considers a scheme of the logistic chain of a fishing-technological cycle of a fishing vessel and a method of a choice of the optimal strategy of fishing vessels relocation under conditions of uncertainty.

title: Trustworthy Multi-Agent AI for Europe: Causal Detection of Instruction Drift, Prompt-Injection Influence, and Communication-Hop Failures Through Counterfactual Diagnostics
authors: Sangam Das
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Agentic Ai Safety How AI Agents Should Talk So the Original Instructions Stay Intact Download the files for the full disclosure. Abstract As artificial intelligence evolves from conversational assistants into distributed networks of autonomous agents, ensuring that originating user instructions retain their intended meaning across communication, delegation, retrieval, and tool execution is becoming a significant technical challenge for trustworthy AI deployment in Europe. An AI agent may receive an authentic and unmodified message yet incorrectly interpret its governing conditions, adopt an unauthorized instruction from lower-trust external content, alter a financial threshold, misapply a temporal requirement, or generate an operation inconsistent with the originating task. Such failures may propagate across multiple agents without revealing which communication or processing boundary first exhibited the discrepancy. Conventional cryptographic integrity verification, agent tracing, output evaluations, and application-level guardrails do not necessarily distinguish legitimate factual influence from unauthorized instruction influence or establish the causal source of an observed deviation. This technical disclosure presents a proposed protocol-independent causal diagnostic architecture for detecting, experimentally testing, and localizing condition-relevant instruction interpretation changes in distributed multi-agent AI systems. The architecture combines versioned typed originating task contracts, source-role and instruction-modification eligibility, message-transformation lineage, controlled factual-versus-instruction counterfactual interventions, adaptive mathematical witness selection, uncertainty-aware behavioral comparison, and evidence-bounded communication-hop localization. A diagnostic witness-selection procedure prioritizes interventions according to expected discrimination between competing fault hypotheses, test execution cost, and mandatory condition coverage. Isolated, non-effectuating diagnostic adapters enable testing across heterogeneous agent communication protocols and tool interfaces without requiring access to proprietary model weights or hidden reasoning states. The resulting evidence distinguishes directly observed message transformations, experimentally supported behavioral influence, and historical causal attribution. When insufficient evidence exists, the architecture reports bounded processing intervals, multiple compatible explanations, or unresolved localization rather than claiming unsupported causal certainty. Additional embodiments support multi-agent branch-and-merge analysis, Time-of-Check-to-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) dependency revalidation, targeted diagnostic corrections, regression testing, and portable evidence packages for independent verification. European regulatory and industrial relevance: The architecture is potentially relevant to the European Union's emphasis on trustworthy, transparent, robust, and accountable AI. Its diagnostic records, traceability mechanisms, uncertainty-qualified findings, and correction-validation procedures may support technical activities associated with the EU AI Act, particularly Articles 12 (record-keeping), 14 (human oversight), and 15 (accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity), where applicable. Data minimization and selective disclosure of diagnostic evidence may also complement GDPR obligations where personal data is processed. Such technical alignment does not itself establish legal compliance. Big Tech and European AI infrastructure alignment: The proposed technology may complement the multi-agent evaluation and observability infrastructure associated with Google Gemini Enterprise and Agent2Agent (A2A), Anthropic Claude and Model Context Protocol (MCP), OpenAI Agents SDK and Codex, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Agent 365, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and European AI development environments including Mistral AI, Aleph Alpha, SAP Business AI, and sovereign or cross-border enterprise AI deployments. Potential industrial applications include diagnosing prompt-injection influence, detecting instruction-authority confusion, identifying communication-hop discrepancies, investigating autonomous-agent failures, validating corrections, and supporting interoperable AI reliability testing across European enterprise and public-sector computing environments. The central technical contribution is the transition from merely detecting incorrect AI-agent outcomes to experimentally distinguishing supported causes, identifying the earliest observable instruction-divergence boundary, and producing independently assessable diagnostic evidence. The proposed architecture offers a potential foundation for improving reliability, interoperability, and technical accountability in distributed agentic AI. Its performance, causal-localization accuracy, and comparative advantages require independent experimental validation.
