title: Celebrating the 70th Anniversary of School of Mechanical Science and Engineering of Huazhong University of Science & Technology
authors: Xinyu Li; Long Wen
abstract: The School of Mechanical Science and Engineering (MSE) of Huazhong University of Science & Technology (HUST-MSE) is one of the best mechanical engineering schools in China. HUST-MSE not only leads the development of equipment automation, digitization and intelligence in China but also wins a high reputation in the field of mechanical engineering in the world. To celebrate the 70th anniversary of HUST-MSE, this special issue aims at presenting the new methodologies and techniques for the application of intelligent manufacturing. This special issue contains seven contributions on the topic areas of manufacturing scheduling, fault diagnosis, automatic welding, and reconfigurable battery systems, which are the important topics in intelligent manufacturing. All the papers are invited from the scholars who were graduated from HUST-MSE. The first paper, ‘an approximate evaluation method for neighbourhood solutions in job shop scheduling problem’ by Gui et al., investigates the approximate evaluation method for the meta-heuristic algorithm solving the Job Shop Scheduling problem. The authors prove that the evaluated value of the neighbourhood solution is under certain conditions by exploring domain knowledge. It can reduce the computational time of the evaluation of meta-heuristics and improve its efficiency. The second paper, ‘a deep reinforcement learning based approach for dynamic distributed blocking flowshop scheduling with job insertions’ by Sun et al., studies the distributed blocking flowshop scheduling problem (DBFSP) with new job insertions. The authors propose a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient method to optimize the job selection model and only make little local modification based on the original plan while minimizing the objective of the total completion time deviation of all products so that all jobs can be finished on time. The third paper, ‘deep reinforcement learning-based balancing and sequencing approach for mixed model assembly lines’ by Lv et al., proposes a multi-agent iterative optimization method for the balancing and sequencing problem in mixed-model assembly lines. The balancing agent adopts a deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm, while the sequencing agent uses an Actor Critic algorithm. Then an iterative interaction mechanism is developed for these agents to minimize the work overload and the idle time at stations. The fourth paper, ‘intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery using lightweight network with modified tree-structured Parzen estimators’ by Liang et al., investigates a novel lightweight network with modified tree-structured Parzen estimators to automatically search the optimal hyper-parameters for the fault diagnosis task. The fifth paper, ‘privacy-preserving gradient boosting tree: vertical federated learning for collaborative bearing fault diagnosis’ by Xia et al., focusses on the insufficient data in real manufacturing scenarios. The authors investigated a vertical federated learning method to break down the data silos while preserving data privacy. Only the model information will be shared for the collaboration to promote its performance. The sixth paper, ‘construction of semi-dense point cloud model for tube-to-tubesheet welding robot’ by Wang et al., aims to promote the tube-to-tubesheet welding and develops a semi-dense point cloud model based on a selected monocular camera and one-dimension laser rangefinder. A laser filtering method is developed firstly to acquire the distance between the camera and the tubesheet, and the tubesheet point cloud model is constructed through the graph optimization algorithm. The seventh paper, ‘reconfigurable battery systems: challenges and safety solutions using intelligent system framework based on digital twins’ by Garg et al., presents an intelligent system framework based on digital twins. The proposed framework is further extended to the life cycle management approach, and it can be helpful to optimize the design, manufacturing, operation, and maintenance of batteries. We appreciate all the authors who have contributed to this special issue. We are also grateful to all the reviewers for their services and commitments to this special issue through their rigorous reviews, timely responses within a tight schedule, and insightful and constructive comments that helped shape the outcome of this issue. All the papers show the good improvements on intelligent manufacturing on the theoretic aspect or the application. Meanwhile, there are still many challenges in the field. The further researches can be conducted on all branches of the collaborative intelligent manufacturing and promote the effectiveness and efficiency of manufacturing systems. We also hope that HUST-MSE is developing better and better.

title: Stochastic Potential Game-Based Target Tracking and Encirclement Approach for Multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles System
authors: Kejie Yang; Ming Zhu; Xiao Guo; Yifei Zhang; Yuting Zhou
abstract: Utilizing fully distributed intelligent control algorithms has enabled the gradual adoption of the multiple unmanned aerial vehicles system for executing Target Tracking and Encirclement missions in industrial and civil applications. Restricted by the evasion behavior of the target, current studies focus on constructing zero-sum game settings, and existing strategy solvers that accommodate continuous state-action spaces have exhibited only modest performance. To tackle the challenges mentioned above, we devise a Stochastic Potential Game framework to model the mission scenario while considering the environment’s limited observability. Furthermore, a multi-agent reinforcement learning method is proposed to estimate the near Nash Equilibrium strategy in the above game scenario, which utilizes time-serial relative kinematic information and obstacle observation. In addition, considering collision avoidance and cooperative tracking, several techniques, such as novel reward functions and recurrent network structures, are presented to optimize the training process. The results of numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits superior search capability for Nash strategies. Moreover, through dynamic virtual experiments conducted with speed and attitude controllers, it has been shown that well-trained actors can effectively act as practical navigators for the real-time swarm control.

title: Deep Learning Optimization for Credit Risk Assessment in Supply Chain Finance Under the Game Theory Framework
authors: Jinzhi Yang
venue: Advances in economics, business and management research/Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research
abstract: Supply chain finance, as a core financial innovation model to alleviate the financing difficulties of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and enhance supply chain coordination efficiency, the accuracy of its credit risk assessment directly determines the safety and sustainability of financial services.Traditional assessment methods have shortcomings such as insufficient characterization of multi-agent game behaviors and weak ability to capture non-linear risk factors.This paper deeply integrates game theory and deep learning to construct an optimized model for credit risk assessment in supply chain finance.Firstly, based on Stackelberg game theory, it analyzes the strategic interaction mechanism among core enterprises, SMEs, and financial institutions, and derives the profit functions and game equilibrium conditions of each agent.Secondly, it designs an Attention-Based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Attention-BiLSTM) model, incorporating key strategic variables obtained from game analysis into the input feature system.Finally, empirical tests are conducted using 5,000 actual transaction data from a supply chain finance platform.The results show that the proposed model is significantly superior to comparison models such as logistic regression and single LSTM in core indicators including accuracy and recall rate, and game features rank among the top in contribution to risk assessment.This study provides interdisciplinary theoretical support and practical solutions for the precise control of credit risks in supply chain finance.

title: Tracking mining company electric vehicles for sustainable development optimization using Distributed Ledger Technologies
authors: Teodora Hristova
abstract: It is established that based on the industrial revolutions towards Industry 5.0, the population of the Earth and its well-being are increasing. To preserve and improve living conditions the development in all spheres of life is by the paradigm of sustainable development. Through the prism of the mining industry, one step could be the introduction of circular economy measures for digitized tracking of materials, repairs, consumed electricity, safety, and finances. Implementing of electric cars is an option to achieve this goal through automation, manageability, and data traceability via Industry 4.0 technologies. Such are blockchain technologies, IoT, V2V, and others. For this purpose, the appropriate types of power supplies for electric vehicles for the mining sector have been identified and information flows have been defined. They are quantity of material, consumed electricity, state of the fleet, charging of batteries and operation of charging stations, and finances. For their implementation, Hyperledger Fabric was chosen as a suitable DLT platform ([1], [2]). Based on Hyperledger Fabric, a conceptual model for tracking material quantities as a step of the circular economy is proposed. A method of communication is shown in the presence of two channels - material and repairs for an electric car.

title: Prosedur Bongkar Muat Peti Kemas dari Kapal KM. Oriental Samudra pada PT. Salam Pacific Indonesia Lines Cabang Medan
authors: Muhammad Wiraromatua Rangkuti; Suratni Ginting; Meriah Kita Deliani
abstract: Container loading and unloading procedures are a series of essential operational activities carried out to systematically, safely, and efficiently move containers from ships to the stacking yard or vice versa. This study aims to examine these procedures, analyze the effectiveness of their implementation, and identify the obstacles and corrective efforts encountered in the field. The methods used include field observation (field research) and literature review (library research). The results indicate that the procedural stages involve document preparation (Bill of Lading and Manifest), ship berthing, the utilization of various loading and unloading equipment (such as Gantry Crane, RTG, and Headtruck), and container arrangement within the Container Yard (CY). The process involves three main work stages: Stevedoring, Cargodoring, and Receiving/Delivery, which require close coordination among port operators, foremen, and Stevedoring Workers (TKBM). Implementation can be hindered by crane breakdowns, headtruck limitations, traffic congestion, and slow stevedoring performance. Effective solutions suggested include routine equipment maintenance, increasing HT fleet capacity, enhancing human resource competency through training, and coordinating traffic routes with relevant authorities. Optimal procedure execution is crucial for ensuring smooth logistics flow, time efficiency, and occupational safety.

title: An Evaluation of Energy Storage Options for Nuclear Power
authors: Justin Leigh Coleman; USDOE Office of Nuclear Energy (NE); Shannon M. Bragg-Sitton; Eric J. Dufek
venue: OSTI OAI (U.S. Department of Energy Office of Scientific and Technical Information)
abstract: Energy supply, distribution, and demand are continuing to evolve as new generation sources come online and new appliances are installed. A larger percentage of the United States (U.S.) energy mix is provided by variable energy sources such as wind and solar each year, and distributed generation is becoming more common. In parallel, an evolution in consumer products such as electrical vehicles, information technology devices for residential and industrial applications, and appliances is changing how energy is consumed. As a result of these trends, nuclear power plants (NPPs) are being called upon to operate more flexibly than ever before. Furthermore, advanced nuclear power plants (A-NPPs) might operate as part of an electricity system that looks very different than when the current NPP fleet was constructed. A-NPPs face the possibility that they will need to operate in an environment where flexibility (e.g., fast ramping) is more highly valued than stability (e.g., baseload generation for conventional demand curves). The current fleet of NPPs is struggling to remain economical in competitive markets in an era of historically low natural gas prices and renewable sources with very low marginal costs. These factors, overlaid with an ambiguous national policy related to nuclear energy and a decision-making context that struggles with multi-decade capital investments, raise key questions and present significant challenges to the economics of nuclear power in the evolving grid. Multiple factors could improve the economics of A-NPPs, including: (1) minimizing the need for active safety systems, (2) minimizing adoption of one-off reactor designs, (3) establishing policies that credit low carbon emitting technologies, and (4) integrating energy storage technologies that increase revenue and reduce costs through a combination of ancillary services, market hedging, and reduced costs via stable operation. This report focuses on Item (4), containing an overview, synthesis, and examination of energy storage options that could be integrated with nuclear generation. Figure 1 provides an overview of the 2015 energy mix by sector, which shows that NPPs are currently used exclusively for electricity generation that is ultimately consumed in the residential, commercial, and industrial sectors. Some areas for NPP energy growth in the future include power generation for electrified transportation and thermal generation for storage and industrial applications. Currently, most industrial thermal energy users combust fossil resources (i.e., coal or natural gas) to meet the energy needs of the processes, but heat from nuclear operations could also be used in certain specific applications.

title: Improvement of aircraft maintenance manual (AMM) for Cessna 172
authors: Tarık Güneş; Uğur Turhan; Birsen Yörük Açıkel
abstract: Purpose This study aims to bring a new approach to the existing structure of Cessna 172 type Aircraft Maintenance Manuals (AMM), operational safety, suitability for maintenance operations and human factors. The purpose of this study is to maintain maintenance operations more safely and effectively. Design/methodology/approach This study tried to develop an approach by using focus group interview and individual interview techniques. At all stages of the study, interviews were made and support was received from the maintenance technicians, technical instructors and students from the aviation industry stakeholders. Findings According to the answers given by the participants, the new approach could have a positive effect on operational safety (98.71%), could have a positive effect on human performance (95.72%) it is understandable (93.16%), it is proper for maintenance operations (88.74%) with high potential to convert into practice (85.92%) and a high potential for future applications (97.06%). Practical implications It can be used in aviation organizations that operate AMM Cessna 172 type aircraft, created with the new approach, in maintenance aircraft maintenance enterprises and maintenance training institutions. Thanks to this approach, aircraft maintenance technicians will be able to perform safely and more effective maintenance activities. Originality/value Contrary to the technologies used by organizations that host wide-body aircraft in their fleets, it requires less cost and less workload to create, use and update. Low-cost airline organizations and maintenance training institutions will also be able to achieve this approach.

title: Governing the Intelligence Loop: Architectural Mitigations for Epistemic Fragility in Autonomous Space-Cyber Threat Analysis
authors: Khadija Taki
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Cyber threats directed against space systems (spanning orbital payloads, tracking and telemetry ground stations, downlinks, and upstream manufacturing supply chains) have evolved into acute operational hazards. Concurrently, national security and commercial defenders face an intelligence volume crisis where telemetry and vulnerability disclosures outpace human cognitive bandwidth. While autonomous multi-agent pipelines powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) offer scalable automation, they introduce severe epistemic liabilities: hallucination, source detachment, uncalibrated certainty, and susceptibility to indirect prompt injection. This paper presents Space-Cyber Brief Crew, a multi-agent cyber threat intelligence (CTI) architecture that automates space-domain intelligence synthesis under an explicit governance layer. Built on a decoupled CrewAI orchestration, the system routes structured reporting through a three-stage sequential pipeline (Collector, Analyst, Writer) governed by ten operational rules. Crucially, the architecture establishes a structural boundary between action capabilities and generative synthesis: downstream analysis agents operate in zero-tool sandboxes, restricting the execution attack surface by construction. We evaluate the framework against a tri-domain threat corpus spanning satellite imagery manipulation, ground industrial control systems (ICS), and global navigation satellite system (GNSS) spoofing. In our evaluation, the governed architecture eliminated identifier fabrication (from 23.3% to 0.0%), preserved 100% provenance retention, and neutralized indirect prompt injection attacks that succeeded in 80% of unconstrained baseline runs. Finally, we examine the institutional, regulatory, and oversight implications, establishing technical criteria for federal procurement and intelligence integration.

title: Admiralty Island in St Petersburg: The Beginning of Development and the First Census of Households
authors: Denis Aleshin; Tatiana A. Bazarova
abstract: This article focuses on the history of the development and settlement of Admiralty Island in St Petersburg in the early eighteenth century. In November 1704, the Admiralty Shipyard was founded, which became the largest shipbuilding enterprise in Russia by the end of the reign of Peter I. Historians agree that the first inhabitants of the island were associated with the fleet and shipbuilding, but the social structure of the population of Admiralty Island, the organisation of construction work and the specifics of administrative management have been studied only fragmentarily. The study is based on published and archival materials from the Admiralty Chancellery and Menshikov’s Field Chancellery (correspondence of construction managers and the first census of buildings), as well as on handwritten drawings. The authors propose a new dating of the manuscript plan of the original Admiralty. It is shown that before the establishment of the Admiralty Chancellery (1707), construction on Admiralty Island was mainly carried out by the forces of the Admiralty Prikaz, which had a cadre of craftsmen and workers. The construction of the Admiralty Fortress was supervised by the St Petersburg Commander-in-Chief R. V. Bruce. Olonets Commander I. Ya. Yakovlev was responsible for the construction of industrial, commercial and residential buildings. Admiralty Island was the first in St Petersburg to begin regulating development. In 1705 residential buildings and barracks were built on Admiralty Island at the expense of the State Treasury. In the early years, a system of prohibitions and restrictions was developed to ensure the safety of shipyards and naval vessels from fire on both Admiralty and City Islands. The study analyses the contents of the building inventories of 1707 and 1711. It shows that their appearance was caused by the need to monitor the implementation of fire safety measures. It is established that in October 1707, the Admiralty officials made an inventory of the buildings on the City Island near the Kronverksky Canal. Analysis of the data from the 1711 inventory shows that at least 110 of the 271 households belonged to naval officers. It is important to note that the census was conducted before the royal court and government moved to the banks of the Neva and before Peter I issued decrees on earth and stone construction and the regulation of development, which changed the appearance of the original St Petersburg.

title: SOA-based distributed fault prognostic and diagnosis framework: An application for preheater cement cyclones
authors: Ouahiba Chouhal
venue: International Journal of Internet Manufacturing and Services
abstract: Complex engineering manufacturing systems require efficient online fault diagnosis methodologies to improve safety and reduce maintenance costs. Traditionally, diagnosis and prognosis approaches are centralised, but these solutions are difficult to implement on distributed systems; whereas a distributed approach of multiple diagnosis and prognosis agents can offer a solution. Also, controlling process plant from a remote location has several benefits including the ability to track and to assist in solving a problem that might arise. This paper presents a distributed and over prognosis and diagnosis approach for physical systems basing on multi agent system and service-oriented architecture. Specifics prognostic and diagnostic procedures and key modules of the architecture for web service-based distributed fault prognostic and diagnosis framework are detailed and developed for the preheater cement cyclones in the workshop of SCIMAT clinker. The experimental case study, reported in the present paper, shows encouraging results and fosters industrial technology transfer.

title: Electric vehicle battery recycling in Brazil: current diagnosis and challenges facing market expansion
authors: João Ricardo Horn Junior; Tiago Markowicz Hable
venue: Institutional Repository of the Federal Technological University of Paraná (RIUT) (Federal University of Technology – Paraná)
abstract: This study analyzes the current structure of the Reverse Logistics (RL) system for Lithium-ion Batteries (LIBs) used in Light Electric Vehicles (LEVs) in Brazil, comparing it with the well-established Lead-acid Battery (LAB) system, which is characterized by high collection rates, consolidated sectoral governance, and economically viable recycling processes. To estimate the future flow of LIBs in the country, historical vehicle registration data from the National Association of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers (ANFAVEA) and the Brazilian Electric Vehicle Association (ABVE) were used and applied to forecasting models based on the Holt-Winters exponential smoothing method, enabling projections of fleet growth and the corresponding volume of end-oflife LIBs. Based on these projections, three prospective scenarios were developed: the first assumes full LIB collection; the second incorporates both collection and secondlife applications; and the third is grounded in the premise of a mature circular economy for these batteries. The scenario analysis indicates the need to develop specific regulatory and operationa frameworks for LIBs in Brazil, given the absence of clear targets, limited infrastructure, and ongoing operational risks, challenges already addressed in international references that provide advanced guidelines for traceability, extended producer responsibility, and critical material recovery. Although informed by the consolidated performance of LABs and by regulatory advances observed in international markets such as the United States and China, this study represents a focused segment within a broader and more complex thematic field: the reverse logistics of LIBs involves technological, environmental, economic and social dimensions that extend beyond the scope adopted here, yet are essential for guiding the development of a robust regulatory framework aligned with safety, traceability and circularity in the sector.

title: ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF RESOURCE FLOW IN CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS THROUGH DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING: A FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCING PROJECT PERFORMANCE IN COMPLEX ENVIRONMENTS
authors: Muhammad Mohiul Islam; ASM Morshed; Md Enamul Kabir; Md Al-Arafat; Precast Plant Manager, JK Builders Sdn Bhd, Johor Bharu, Malaysia.
venue: American Journal of Scholarly Research and Innovation
abstract: The advancements in Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) are transforming construction project management, particularly in resource allocation, scheduling, and risk mitigation. Traditional heuristic-based methods struggle with dynamic project environments, necessitating AI-driven approaches. This systematic review, following PRISMA guidelines, evaluates 482 peer-reviewed studies to assess the effectiveness of DRL in optimizing construction workflows. Findings reveal that DRL-based workforce allocation reduces idle time by 30% and enhances labor productivity by 35%, while DRL-driven equipment utilization improves efficiency by 40% and reduces downtime by 28%. Additionally, material logistics optimization through DRL decreases procurement delays and waste by 30%, significantly improving supply chain management. Risk-sensitive DRL models outperform Monte Carlo simulations, reducing cost overruns by 27% and improving risk prediction accuracy by 30%. Comparative analysis confirms that DRL scheduling frameworks, including Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Deep Q Networks (DQN), and Actor-Critic models, improve project efficiency by 32%, surpassing traditional CPM and PERT methods. Simulation-based studies further validate that DRL-driven decision-making reduces discrepancies in resource utilization by 21%, while IoT-integrated DRL improves safety compliance by 38% and reduces accident risks by 35%. Despite computational challenges, DRL offers scalability, adaptability, and superior automation, making it a powerful tool for intelligent construction management. This review highlights gaps in empirical validation, AI adoption frameworks, and multi-agent DRL applications, emphasizing the need for further research and industry integration to enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and mitigate risks in construction projects.

title: Performance, Adaptability, and Security in AI-Driven IIoT: A Survey
authors: Uddin Md. Borhan; Arif Raza; Taki Uddin; Mahbubul Islam; A.K.M. Muzahidul Islam; Jie Chen
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) integrates cyber-physical systems, edge-cloud computing, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and advanced connectivity to enable intelligent, data-driven operations across manufacturing, energy, transportation, and healthcare. The convergence of Operational Technology (OT) and Information Technology (IT), together with pervasive AI-driven automation, complicates meeting the joint requirements of performance, adaptability, and security (PAS). This survey adopts an explicitly AI-centric view of PAS and reviews IIoT research spanning deep reinforcement learning (DRL), multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), digital twins (DTs), federated and collaborative learning, graph neural networks (GNNs), blockchain-assisted analytics, and lightweight and post-quantum cryptography. The reviewed approaches are analyzed across device, edge, fog, cloud, and application layers under industrial constraints such as latency, reliability, resource limits, safety requirements, and regulatory compliance. A PAS-centric taxonomy is introduced that links technique families to deployment layers and application domains, and recurring trade-offs among PAS dimensions are summarized. Open challenges are identified in multi-objective optimization, semantic interoperability, lifecycle validation, and governance, with directions outlined toward secure and sustainable Industry 5.0 IIoT ecosystems.

title: Safe Drive+: Real-Time Driver Health Monitoring System
authors: MIRZA SHERIFF; ANDREW BLESSING J; NAGAMANIKAM JAGADEEP R; THOUFEEQ TR; SIVASHANKAR B
venue: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
abstract: Road accidents involving heavy vehicles are frequently associated with sudden driver health emergencies such as cardiac arrest, hypoxia, heat stress, and fatigue-related complications. Conventional monitoring approaches including wearable devices and camera-based driver monitoring systems often suffer from low compliance, poor environmental adaptability, and unreliable detection accuracy. This paper presents Safe Drive+ 2.0, a multi-point, real time driver health monitoring system integrated directly into the steering wheel, driver’s seat, and seat belt of heavy vehicles. The system employs pressure sensors and IR proximity sensors to ensure vital sign monitoring is activated only when the driver is present and properly positioned. The steering wheel integrates the MAX30102 sensor for heart rate (HR) and oxygen saturation (SpO₂) measurement. Temperature sensors (LM35/DS18B20) embedded in the seat monitor body and cabin temperature. The seat belt provides redundancy through fastening detection and additionalcontact sensing. An ESP32 microcontroller processes sensor data and compares it against medically validated thresholds recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and the American Heart Association (AHA). When abnormal parameters are detected (SpO₂ ≤ 90%, HR 120 bpm, body temperature 38.6°C), a two-step safety protocol is initiated: (1) local alert via buzzer and RGB LED; (2) automatic GSM-based SMS alert with GPS location if unacknowledged. Sensor data is logged to an SD card for post-trip analytics.The system operates on a regulated 12/24V vehicle supply with surge protection, ensuring reliability in harsh environments. Safe Drive+ 2.0 provides a low cost, retrofit-friendly, IoT-enabled solution for trucks, buses, and industrial vehicles, enhancing fleet safety and proactive driver health management. Key Words: Driver Health Monitoring, Heavy Vehicle Safety, IoT in Transportation, MAX30102, ESP32, GSM Alert System, SpO₂ Monitoring, Fleet Safety, Embedded Systems, Real-Time Monitoring

title: Toward Efficient Utilization of Low-Altitude Airspace: A Unified Approach Integrating Architecture Frameworks and Operations Research
authors: Wentian Chen; Lefei Li
abstract: This article presents a unified approach that integrates the unified architecture framework (UAF) with operations research to automate design and optimization of low-altitude airspace systems of systems. We extend the UAF domain metamodel with lightweight stereotypes within strategic, operational, service, resource, and actual resource views. An optimization bridge view generates solver-neutral mixed-integer linear programming models that minimize mission time while enforcing explicit energy budget and safety separation constraints and feeds the optimization results back into the architecture for iterative refinement. We validate the methodology on a 1,000-case urban logistics scenario by formulating a multidepot heterogeneous fleet vehicle routing problem (MDHFVRP) directly from the architecture models. The baseline architecture yields a mean operating time of 23.32 min, meeting the service target in 72.75% of cases. Introducing a moving-depot extension and solving the resulting moving MDHFVRP with a gradient-guided large-neighborhood search reduce the mean to 21.20 min, achieving the target in 96.09% of scenarios at a median solve time of 10.88 s. The coupled pipeline preserves full traceability from strategic goals to detailed optimization outputs and supports rapid tradeoff analysis and bottleneck diagnosis.

title: Integrated Boiler Automation on Siemens S7-400 and PCS7 Platform
authors: Bangjie Xu
abstract: Integrated automation and closed-loop regulation of a natural- circulation boiler are built across the Siemens PCS7 and S7-400 stack, exercised on the SMPT-1000 high-fidelity unit.Addressing the inherent complexities of boiler dynamics—including strong coupling, nonlinearity, and significant time delays—the research focuses on the boiler unit within the Synthesis Multi-Functional Process Training System (SMPT-1000). Grounded in the thermal-flow topology of the SMPT-1000 unit, the regulatory architecture is assembled to hold industrial safety margins and tight parameter tolerances. The build wires Continuous Function Charts (CFC) for advanced closed-loop regulation, Sequential Function Charts (SFC) for deterministic operational logic, and a full WinCC Human– Machine Interface (HMI) for live process visualization. Comparative runs on the SMPT-1000 model show the assembled stack suppressing external upset while drum level and main steam pressure stay inside their service bands, outperforming conventional PID baselines on dynamic settling and steady-state variance. The same module layout reads as a scalable engineering template for intelligent automation and digital retrofits across industrial boiler fleets.

title: Human-AI trust for safer heavy-duty equipment management: Insights from socio-technical literature review and interviews
authors: Ava Jahanbiglari; Seongeun Park; Erin K. Chiou; Pingbo Tang
abstract: Heavy-duty equipment management increasingly relies on AI-enabled cyber-physical systems integrating sensors and digital twins to improve safety, efficiency, and sustainability. Despite technical advances, field deployment remains limited, suggesting adoption barriers driven more by socio-technical misalignment among intelligent systems, organizational processes, and human decision-making than by algorithmic capability. Accordingly, trust between humans and intelligent systems shapes whether automation yields operational gains. This review synthesizes 90 papers and four expert interviews across construction, logistics, and fleet management using bibliometric mapping and thematic synthesis. Although cross-domain in scope, the evidence base is construction-dominant and offers transferable insights for broader equipment management. Guided by socio-technical systems and relational trust-in-automation theories, this synthesis identified five socio-technical pillars: human-technology interaction; workforce adaptation; data quality, integration, and scarcity; decision-making under uncertainty; and operational efficiency. Across these pillars, recurring constraints to AI-enabled system deployment include surveillance perceptions, trailer power/connectivity limits, and fragmented manufacturer portals, motivating a trust-centered framework.

title: Architectural Resilience in AI-Driven Decision Systems under Adversarial Conditions
authors: Viswapriyan Ragupathy
venue: IEEE International Conference on AI in Cybersecurity (ICAIC)
abstract: The Self-Healing AI Architecture shows that resilient cognitive layers improve multi-agent AI systems' stability, autonomy and dependability. The method decreases recovery latency, cross-agent failure propagation and accuracy retention across failure scenarios with minimal operating overhead. Structured recovery patterns such as Semantic Checkpointing, Cognitive Rollback, Quarantine Isolation and Adaptive Consensus Reset enable systematic reasoning-level degradations, and empirical validation across 20 cooperative agents proves the architecture's scalability and enterprise suitability. These findings emphasise cognitive-layer robustness for reliable agentic AI. Several architectural upgrades are planned. In predictive fault models, time-series analysis and anomaly detection may enable proactive recovery before reasoning fails. Reinforcement learning–based optimisation may choose experience-based recovery approaches under changing situations. Vision, reinforcement learning, and symbolic agents enhance application beyond LLM-based agents. Cognitive-layer, infrastructure-level resilience, and formal verification may improve large-scale deployment accuracy and safety.

title: Hydrogen CPS Digital-Twin IDS Dataset
authors: Yavari A.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This dataset contains multivariate time-series measurements representing a hydrogen logistics cyber–physical system that integrates cryogenic storage/transfer operations, SCADA/PLC control, IIoT sensing, fleet logistics telemetry, and cybersecurity network indicators. It is designed to support research on joint cyber intrusion detection and physical safety monitoring under a digital-twin–enabled operating setting, where simulated twin states and real process states may diverge during abnormal events. Each row corresponds to one timestamped observation from a sensor/terminal/tanker context. The dataset includes (i) raw operational signals (pressure, temperatures, flow, vibration), (ii) control and authentication signals from industrial automation, (iii) network/security behavior indicators, (iv) digital-twin synchronization variables, and (v) engineered cross-domain risk indices. The dataset supports both multi-class intrusion classification and continuous leakage severity estimation. title: Réseaux d'Oscillateurs Hiérarchiques Multi-Échelles Formalisation Dynamique, Analyse Spectrale et Stabilité Structurelle
authors: Kevin FRADIER
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: . Réseaux d’Oscillateurs Hiérarchiques Multi-Échelles Formalisation Dynamique, Analyse Spectrale et Stabilité Structurelle Kevin Fradier © 2025 Kevin Fradier — Creative Commons Attribution - Pas d’Utilisation Commerciale - Pas de Modification 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) Résumé Nous proposons une architecture hiérarchique de réseaux d’oscillateurs non linéaires intégrant une séparation explicite des échelles temporelles. Le modèle repose sur une extension structurée du cadre de Kuramoto, incluant des couplages intra- et inter-niveaux organisés de manière stratifiée. Nous démontrons : l’existence de régimes de synchronisation partielle, la stabilité locale sous conditions spectrales, la présence d’attracteurs invariants hiérarchisés, une robustesse aux perturbations stochastiques bornées. L’ensemble est formalisé dans le cadre des systèmes dynamiques sur variétés compactes, avec analyse énergétique et spectrale. Le modèle constitue une base théorique pour des systèmes distribués adaptatifs multi-agents. 1. Introduction Les systèmes complexes distribués présentent fréquemment : organisation hiérarchique, dynamique multi-échelles, coordination émergente sans supervision centrale. Ce travail formalise une architecture mathématique minimale capable de reproduire ces propriétés. L’objectif est strictement dynamique et analytique :proposer un cadre cohérent, testable et généralisable. 2. Définition du Modèle 2.1 Structure On considère N oscillateurs répartis en trois niveaux : S0 : dynamique rapide S1 : dynamique intermédiaire S2 : dynamique lente Chaque oscillateur est défini par une phase θᵢ(t) ∈ S¹. L’espace d’état global est un tore N-dimensionnel compact. 2.2 Dynamique Générale Pour chaque oscillateur : dθᵢ/dt = ωᵢ somme des couplages intra-niveau somme pondérée des couplages inter-niveaux Les interactions sont de type sinusoïdal (structure Kuramoto généralisée). 2.3 Hypothèses Structurantes H1 : fréquences propres bornéesH2 : matrices de couplage intra-niveau symétriques et connexesH3 : couplages inter-niveaux bornésH4 : séparation stricte des échelles temporellesH5 : perturbations stochastiques éventuelles de variance finie Ces hypothèses garantissent existence, unicité et bornitude des trajectoires. 3. Analyse Spectrale La linéarisation autour d’un état synchronisé conduit à une dynamique gouvernée par le laplacien du graphe hiérarchique. Condition clé : La plus petite valeur propre non nulle du laplacien (λ₂) doit être strictement positive. Conséquences : cohérence locale stable, convergence exponentielle, robustesse structurelle. 4. Analyse Énergétique On définit une fonctionnelle : E(Θ) = − somme pondérée des cosinus des différences de phase. Sous symétrie des couplages : dE/dt ≤ 0 Le système possède donc : une dynamique dissipative, des attracteurs correspondant à des minima locaux, une organisation spontanée. 5. Dynamique Multi-Échelles La séparation des échelles permet une réduction dimensionnelle : les niveaux rapides convergent vers une variété lente, les niveaux lents modulent cette variété. On obtient un système réduit gouvernant la dynamique globale. Ce cadre s’inscrit dans la théorie des systèmes singulièrement perturbés. 6. Théorèmes Principaux Théorème 1 — Cohérence Locale Sous H1–H3, il existe un seuil critique de couplage assurant la stabilité locale d’un état synchronisé partiel. Théorème 2 — Stabilité Hiérarchique Sous H1–H4, le système admet une variété lente attractive, garantissant la cohérence multi-niveaux. Ces résultats reposent sur : linéarisation locale, analyse du spectre du laplacien, théorie de Lyapunov, réduction singulière. 7. Robustesse Stochastique Avec bruit additif borné : dθ = dynamique déterministe + σ ξ(t) La stabilité dépend du rapport : couplage / variance du bruit. La hiérarchie améliore la tolérance aux perturbations comparée à un réseau homogène équivalent. 8. Extension vers Réseaux Adaptatifs On peut introduire une dynamique lente des couplages : dKᵢⱼ/dt proportionnelle à la corrélation des phases. Cela transforme le modèle en réseau auto-adaptatif avec attracteurs évolutifs. Applications potentielles : apprentissage distribué, coordination robotique, systèmes multi-agents. 9. Falsifiabilité Le modèle serait remis en question si : aucune synchronisation n’apparaît au-delà du seuil critique, la séparation d’échelle ne stabilise pas le système, le spectre du laplacien ne corrèle pas avec la cohérence observée, la fonction énergétique n’est pas monotone. Le cadre est donc empiriquement testable. 10. Limites Le modèle : ne représente aucun système biologique spécifique, ne valide aucune interprétation historique, ne constitue pas une théorie universelle des systèmes complexes. Il est un cadre mathématique abstrait. 11. Conclusion Nous avons formalisé un réseau hiérarchique multi-échelles d’oscillateurs non linéaires présentant : attracteurs cohérents, stabilité spectrale, dissipation énergétique, robustesse structurelle, généralisabilité. Le cadre est : analytiquement encadré, numériquement simulable, structurellement cohérent, scientifiquement défendable. Il constitue une base pour le développement de systèmes distribués adaptatifs formellement justifiés. title: Mathematical Modeling of Combined Vessel Loading-Unloading Operations by a Group of Quay Cranes in a Stochastic Environment
authors: Victor Shchyrba; Тетяна Пилипюк; Mykola Shynkaryk
venue: International Conference on Advanced Computer Information Technologies (ACIT)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of integrated resource management at a container terminal under conditions of high vessel handling intensity. A multifactor mathematical model for synchronizing a group of quay cranes operating on shared rails is developed and theoretically substantiated. Unlike existing solutions, the model integrates dynamic nonintersection constraints and ground transport fleet capacity with real-time vessel hydrostatics and stability parameters within a single multi-stream architecture. This optimization ensures that high-intensity combined loading and unloading operations strictly adhere to safety margins for the vessel's vertical center of gravity, heel, and trim. Special attention is paid to the concept of “vertical slot”, where optimizing the order of access to the vessel's cells minimizes idle movements of the crane trolley. The model's study based on three cranes confirmed the possibility of reducing the total vessel handling time and minimizing ballast water pumping requirements. This is achieved by eliminating mutual locking of equipment, preventing violations of the vessel's stability and equalizing the load on the terminal's logistics network. The proposed approach improves coordination efficiency of quay crane operations, reduces idle time, and enhances overall terminal throughput, demonstrating its practical applicability for decision support in container terminal management under uncertainty.

title: Research on the evolutionary control of unsafe behavior of construction personnel based on multi-field coupled-homogeneous analysis model
authors: Haoran Zhao; Changfeng Wang; Qiushuang Zheng; Xuefeng Xia; Yanmin Ouyang
abstract: Unsafe behavior among construction personnel poses significant risks in petroleum engineering construction projects. This study addresses this issue through the application of a multi-field coupled homogeneous analysis model. By conducting case analyses of petroleum engineering construction accidents and utilizing the WSR methodology, the influencing factors of unsafe behaviors among construction personnel are systematically categorized into organizational system factors, equipment management factors, and construction personnel factors. Subsequently, employing Risk coupling theory, the study delves into the analysis of these influencing factors, discussing their coupling mechanisms and classifications, and utilizing the N-K model to elucidate the coupling effect among them. Furthermore, a novel approach integrating coupling analysis and multi-agent modeling is employed to establish an evolutionary model of construction personnel's unsafe behavior. The findings reveal that a two-factor control method, concurrently reinforcing equipment and construction personnel management, significantly mitigates unsafe behavior. This study provides valuable insights into the evolution of unsafe behavior among construction personnel and offers a robust theoretical framework for targeted interventions. Significantly, it bears practical implications for guiding safety management practices within petroleum engineering construction enterprises. By effectively controlling unsafe behaviors and implementing targeted safety interventions, it contributes to fostering sustainable development within the petroleum engineering construction industry.

title: ARISE: Autonomous Reconfigurable Infrastructure for Swarm-based Exploration
authors: Harish Vernekar
venue: UA Campus Repository (The University of Arizona)
abstract: Over the coming decade, activity in the near-Earth environment will expand from a handful of missions into dense cislunar and geostationary networks: communication relays and positioning services, logistics traffic, and sustained operations on and around the Moon. That build-out calls for a deep, persistent surveillance and communication layer, one able to monitor in-orbit and surface operations across the Earth-Moon system, not just a few assets at a time. The infrastructure meant to provide that view is not keeping pace: debris populations keep growing, the traffic they threaten keeps rising, and the cancellation of the Lunar Gateway has removed the one crewed platform that would have watched this expansion fromlunar orbit. Meeting that need calls for infrastructure that is itself distributed, autonomous, and reusable. Small spacecraft flown in coordinated swarms can spread sensing and relay across a whole domain, but only if they can be deployed, operated without a human in the loop, recovered, and flown again. This thesis develops ARISE, an Autonomous Reconfigurable Infrastructure for Swarm-based Exploration: a carrier-and-deputy CubeSat architecture designed for exactly that lifecycle. A carrier delivers and later recovers a fleet of deputies, and that fleet can be resized, reconfigured, and reused across missions rather than expended on a single mission. The heart of the contribution is the autonomy that a reusable, unattended fleet requires. ARISE couples a rigorous, certificate-backed deployment layer with an onboard fault detection, isolation, and recovery system and an autonomous redocking capability that returns each deputy to its carrier for refueling and re-flight. Built on formally assured monitoring and safety logic, the fleet can separate, hold station, survive faults, and come home with no operator on the line. Framed this way, ARISE is a scalable, reusable path toward rapid-response reconnaissance of newly discovered hazardous objects, multi-perspective small-body science, and the distributed surveillance of a cislunar and geostationary domain that now lacks its intended platforms. To evaluate the architecture end-to-end, the thesis drives it through the most demanding near-term opportunity of the decade: the close flyby of asteroid (99942) Apophis on 13 April 2029, when the body passes within the geostationary ring, closer than many operational spacecraft. A single ESPA-class carrier releases 8 6U deputies to fixed stations around the asteroid to image a fast, once-only encounter, with the object sweeping past at 8.76 km/s and resolvable for only a few seconds. The design meets that window’s two hard constraints, lighting the dark hemisphere with co-boresighted strobes and freezing the motion with a fixed inertial stare, and a high-fidelity, statistically sampled analysis confirms near-complete whole-body coverage along with the autonomy to deploy, survive, and recover the fleet. It is one concrete instance of the reusable, swarm-based infrastructure the coming decade of cislunar and geostationary operations will demand.

title: Automation of the Planning Phase of a Construction Project Using AI Agents
authors: Bartosz Korba; Katarzyna Pawluk
abstract: The chronic digitalisation deficit within the construction sector induces design anomalies and human errors, leading to a severe erosion of investment profitability. This study aims to implement the automation of resource generation and validation processes, acting as a systemic safety barrier to stabilise analytical workflows. The proposed methodology relies on a Multi-Agent System (MAS) architecture embedded within the n8n environment and powered by Gemini-class language models. The framework integrates a deterministic PostgreSQL database within a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, enabling the precise, real-time processing of Construction Law regulations. Applying Chain-of-Thought reasoning alongside structured prompt templates helped eliminate model logic drift, ensuring comprehensive result reproducibility. The deployment of this platform induced a 96% acceleration in the pre-construction phase, reducing the formulation time of Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)/Critical Path Method (CPM) structures from a baseline of 480 min to an average of 20 min. The empirical data demonstrates a radical compression of operational costs (OPEX) concurrent with the marginalisation of the Human Error Probability (HEP) index to a residual level of < 1%. Ultimately, the solution drastically minimised the iterative overhead, confining the design cycle to a single execution while maintaining high level of compliance with the 7R (7 Rights) Logistics Directive.

title: The Convergence of AI and Low-Altitude Economy
authors: Zhongyi Wang; Shuzhi Liu; Yusen Liu
venue: International Conference on Information and Communication Technology Convergence (ICTC)
abstract: The low-altitude economy, as a national strategic emerging industry utilizing airspace below 1,000 meters (extendable to 3,000 meters in specific scenarios) as its operational platform, is rapidly developing and projected to reach a market size of 2 trillion yuan by 2030. Artificial intelligence (AI) technology, as a key enabling technology, is driving the transformation of the low-altitude economy from traditional applications to intelligent and autonomous operations. This paper systematically analyzes the current state and development trends of the integration of AI and the low-altitude economy from three aspects: technical framework, application scenarios, and challenges. First, we propose a four-layer technical architecture comprising perception, cognition, decision-making, and execution layers, and elaborate on core technologies such as multi-agent collaborative control, knowledge graphs and semantic compression, and airspace intelligent management. Then, we analyze the implementation effects of AI technologies in typical application scenarios such as logistics and distribution, urban governance, emergency rescue, and cultural tourism and education. Finally, we discuss challenges including safety risks, regulatory policies, and technical bottlenecks, and propose corresponding development recommendations. Through analysis of existing literature and practical cases, this paper provides theoretical reference and practical guidance for the deep integration of the low-altitude economy and AI.

title: Art and industry
authors: Neil Drabble; Rose Gridneff
abstract: The relationship between art and design practice and the skills, techniques and processes required to make work is one that is intrinsically connected to the physicality of the spaces of the art school ecosystem. Each discipline – from fashion to furniture design – requires a discrete material knowledge that is supported by workshops to enable the exploration of processes and the production of artefacts. These range from the ceramics workshop, through to skills that are rooted in industry such as commercial typesetting and printing. These invariably differ from institution to institution, with a distinction that can be drawn between colleges that historically taught fine art practice and those whose origins lie within technical schools. The regional priorities of Britain’s industrial heritage is evidenced nationally, from the weaving sheds at Bury School of Art that provided education for mill workers in Lancashire, to London College of Printing (now Communication) that trained apprentices for Fleet Street. 1 Workshops today are a complex mix of what has been actively preserved from previous eras – or in some cases, what has been left behind, as it was too problematic to move due to heavy or specialist equipment. These now rub shoulders with workshops and maker spaces that support newer and emergent technologies, providing students with the opportunity to seamlessly work across the analogue and the digital.

title: Crystal Oscillator Product Solutions
authors: XtalTQ
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Crystal Oscillator Product Solutions for Aerospace, Communications, Industrial, Medical, IoT, and Positioning Applications Crystal Oscillator Product Solutions for Precision Frequency Control Crystal oscillators are essential timing components used across modern electronic systems. Their ability to deliver precise, stable, and reliable frequency signals makes them indispensable in industries where accuracy, synchronization, and long-term performance matter. From aerospace navigation and 5G communications to medical diagnostics, industrial automation, IoT connectivity, and positioning systems, crystal oscillator solutions provide the timing foundation that keeps advanced technologies operating correctly. As electronic devices become faster, smarter, and more connected, the demand for high-performance frequency control continues to grow. Engineers require oscillators that not only meet standard electrical specifications but also satisfy industry-specific needs such as low phase noise, ultra-low jitter, compact size, low power consumption, wide temperature operation, and rugged environmental reliability. A well-designed crystal oscillator product solution helps improve system stability, reduce signal errors, support accurate data processing, and enhance overall product performance. What Is a Crystal Oscillator? A crystal oscillator is an electronic circuit that uses the mechanical resonance of a quartz crystal to generate a stable electrical signal. Quartz crystals vibrate at a highly predictable frequency when electrical energy is applied. This natural stability allows crystal oscillators to serve as accurate clock sources for electronic circuits. Crystal controlled oscillators are used for medical because they offer: High frequency stability Excellent timing accuracy Low jitter performance Low phase noise options Long-term reliability Compact package availability Compatibility with digital and RF systems Depending on the application, engineers may select different oscillator types, including standard crystal oscillators, temperature-compensated crystal oscillators, voltage-controlled crystal oscillators, oven-controlled crystal oscillators, and ultra-low-power oscillator solutions. Why Crystal Oscillator Solutions Matter Across Industries Every electronic system needs timing. A processor needs a clock to execute instructions. A radio needs a reference frequency to transmit and receive signals. A medical scanner needs synchronized timing to acquire accurate data. A GPS receiver needs precise timekeeping to calculate position. Industrial controllers need stable clocks to coordinate sensors and actuators. When timing quality is poor, systems can suffer from data errors, unstable communication, measurement inaccuracy, weak signal integrity, and reduced reliability. Crystal oscillator product solutions help avoid these problems by delivering accurate and dependable frequency references. Different industries have different priorities. Aerospace and defense systems may demand ruggedized oscillators with high shock resistance. IoT devices may require miniature, low-power timing solutions. Communication networks may need low phase noise and low jitter. Medical equipment may prioritize stability, precision, and reliability. This is why application-specific crystal oscillator solutions are so important. Crystal Oscillator for Positioning Systems Precision Timing for Navigation and Location Tracking Positioning systems depend on accurate time measurement. Technologies such as GPS, GNSS, asset tracking devices, navigation modules, fleet management systems, drones, and precision agriculture equipment all rely on stable timing references. A crystal oscillator for positioning provides the accurate frequency needed to calculate time differences between transmitted and received signals. Even small timing errors can result in significant location inaccuracies. A stable oscillator helps positioning systems maintain reliable performance, especially in environments where signal conditions change. Key benefits for positioning applications include: Accurate timekeeping Reliable GNSS performance Improved location accuracy Stable operation across temperature changes Low power options for portable trackers Support for navigation and timing synchronization For high-accuracy positioning systems, temperature stability and low phase noise may become critical design factors. Crystal Oscillator for Communications and Enterprise Networks Reliable Data Transmission and Network Synchronization The communications and enterprise sectors rely heavily on crystal oscillators for timing synchronization and frequency control. Network infrastructure, routers, switches, servers, optical modules, wireless base stations, and telecom systems all require stable clocks to manage high-speed data flow. A crystal oscillator for communications helps maintain signal integrity and reduce data errors. In high-speed networks, timing uncertainty can create packet loss, bit errors, latency problems, or synchronization failures. Important oscillator requirements in communications include: Low jitter for high-speed data links Low phase noise for RF signal quality Stable frequency over temperature Strong long-term aging performance Compatibility with Ethernet, optical, and wireless systems Reliable operation in enterprise and telecom environments With the expansion of 5G, fiber optic networks, cloud computing, and data centers, precise timing has become even more important. Crystal oscillator solutions support the synchronization that keeps digital communication fast, stable, and secure. Crystal Oscillator for Instruments Precision Timing for Measurement and Control Equipment Instrumentation systems require high accuracy and repeatability. Oscilloscopes, signal generators, spectrum analyzers, frequency counters, laboratory instruments, industrial meters, and test platforms all depend on accurate frequency references. A crystal oscillator for instruments provides the stable clock signal needed for measurement accuracy. If the reference clock drifts or produces excessive noise, the instrument may deliver unreliable results. Crystal oscillator is commonly used in instruments often emphasize: High frequency accuracy Low phase noise Low jitter Excellent temperature stability Long-term reliability Consistent measurement performance In precision measurement, the quality of the timing source directly affects the quality of the data. High-performance oscillator solutions help engineers, researchers, and manufacturers obtain dependable results. Crystal Oscillator for Industrial and Medical Applications Stable Timing for Automation, Control, and Diagnostics Industrial and medical systems require reliable timing in environments where accuracy and uptime are critical. In industrial applications, crystal oscillators support automation systems, robotics, PLCs, sensors, motor controllers, smart meters, industrial Ethernet, and machine monitoring equipment. They help synchronize sensors, actuators, controllers, and communication modules to improve process control and operational efficiency. In medical applications, crystal oscillators support diagnostic systems, imaging equipment, patient monitors, laboratory analyzers, portable medical devices, and digital healthcare platforms. Stable timing enables accurate data acquisition, signal processing, and device coordination. A crystal oscillator for industrial and medical applications must often provide: Strong temperature stability Low noise performance High reliability Compact size Low power consumption Resistance to vibration and interference Long operating life Medical devices may also require miniature and energy-efficient oscillators for portable or wearable use. Industrial systems may need rugged timing components capable of operating in harsh conditions with temperature fluctuations, vibration, and electromagnetic noise. Crystal Oscillator for Space and Defense Mission-Critical Timing in Extreme Environments Space and defense applications place some of the highest demands on crystal oscillator technology. Satellites, avionics, radar systems, secure radios, missile guidance systems, navigation platforms, electronic warfare systems, and aerospace instruments all depend on precise and reliable timing. A crystal oscillator for space and defense must maintain stable performance under extreme conditions, including shock, vibration, radiation exposure, temperature extremes, and electromagnetic interference. Key requirements often include: Exceptional frequency stability Low phase noise for radar and RF systems Ruggedized package design Wide temperature operation High shock and vibration tolerance Long-term reliability Mission-critical quality standards In satellite communications, oscillators help maintain stable links between spacecraft and ground stations. In radar systems, low phase noise improves detection accuracy. In navigation and guidance systems, precise timing supports accurate position, velocity, and trajectory calculations. For mission-critical environments, oscillator failure is not acceptable. High-reliability crystal oscillator solutions help ensure operational safety and mission success. Crystal Oscillator for IoT Applications Ultra-Low Power Timing for Connected Devices The Internet of Things has created massive demand for compact, low-power, and cost-effective timing components. IoT devices often operate on batteries and communicate wirelessly, so they need oscillators that deliver stable timing while consuming minimal energy. A crystal oscillator for IoT applications supports smart sensors, wearables, asset trackers, smart home devices, wireless modules, environmental monitors, industrial IoT nodes, and connected healthcare devices.

title: Venetian Shipping from the Days of Glory to Decline, 1453–1571, by Renard Gluzman
authors: Nicola Carotenuto
abstract: Renard Gluzman has written an essential contribution to the history of Venetian shipping in the late medieval and early modern period, spanning several centuries, and providing an up-to-date account of Venetian ships and shipping, alongside an eco-history of sixteenth-century Venice. The book is the product of eight years of research undertaken by the author for his doctoral dissertation, which was awarded the Ugo Tucci Prize by the Istituto Veneto di Scienze, Lettere ed Arti. The book is divided into three parts, each devoted to a separate topic. The first, titled, ‘The Legal, Executive, and Judicial Framework’, investigates Venice’s sea laws, with respect to the identification of Venetian ships, the regulative powers of Venetian authorities over shipping, the division of ships into classes, the assessment of volume and size, safety rules and imposts. The second part, ‘Shipping Enterprise and the World of Round Ships’, deals both with the biographies of ships, highlighting their life-spans and characteristics, and with the maritime enterprise, assessing profitability and explaining the organisational structure of the shipping business. The third section, ‘Venetian Shipping During the Commercial Revolution Reconsidered’, presents a painstakingly detailed history of Venetian shipping from 1423 to 1571, alongside an eco-history of the lagoon in the same period. The book is further enriched by six appendices, presenting snapshots of Venice’s merchant marine, estimates of the size of four colonial fleets, the itinerary and life expectancy of certain round ships, the cost of construction of vessels, and net and gross incomes from freight.

title: To Study Commercial Vehicle and Customer Satisfaction: Meeting Customer Needs in the Commercial Vehicle Industry
authors: Dr. Prakash H. Karmadkar Dr. Prakash H. Karmadkar
venue: Journal of Advances and Scholarly Researches in Allied Education
abstract: Unlike personal or business cars, Commercial vehicles are mainly utilized for business purpose, When we travel across India we realize that even two wheelers are modified to carry the load. Best examples are ‘Chhakada’ which are used in Gujrat, converted from Rajdoot motor cycle. Three wheelers have their own limitations in terms of speed and load carrying capacity. These are very basic on safety and in terms of style statements. Exactly this chord was captured by Tata Motors while introducing ACE and world has experienced the change that was brought by ACE. Small truck of three wheeler to four wheel added to prestige of the owner. In India, there are two types of truck customers. One who owns it and driven by his driver while on the other hand owner himself is driver. First one is called as fleet owner, hence, needs of fleet owner and owner cum driver differs on many aspects, while essential requirements or basic requirements remains same. title: Determination of Quality of Works on Maintenance and Repair of Rolling Stock of Motor Transport
authors: Пернебеков Сакен Садибекович; Dinara Tortbayeva; Ussen Ussipbayev; Baurzhan Shoibekov; А.O. Kazenova
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
abstract: The relevance of the topic stated in this research is conditioned by modern trends in the economic development of the Republic of Kazakhstan, associated with the increasing importance of road transport in the infrastructure of the country and the associated need for objective monitoring of its current technical condition. The purpose of this work is to study the principles of determining the quality of maintenance and improving the technical operation of road vehicles in Kazakhstan. Methodologically, the research involved a practical analysis of techniques to improve technical operations and assess service quality for GAZ 33-02 (mileage 120,000-150,000 km) and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter (mileage 160,000-180,000 km) vehicles through monitoring a number of routine service operations. The findings reveal specific opportunities to enhance vehicle maintenance quality at car service enterprises. The research indicates that using high-quality equipment and materials during repairs significantly improves the technical operation of road transport fleets. Additionally, it was determined that to optimize technical operations for the vehicles studied, basic maintenance should be conducted every 15,000-20,000 km of its mileage, with thorough inspections of all critical components to ensure safety. This will allow the rolling stock of road transport to be maintained at the proper level of readiness for operation for as long as possible, provided that its repair costs are minimized. The practical significance of the results of this research lies in the possibility of their use in planning the activities of road transport enterprises in Kazakhstan aimed at the maintenance and repair of vehicles.

title: A Comparative Study of Unsupervised Machine Learning Methods for Anomaly Detection in Flight Data: Case Studies from Real-World Flight Operations
authors: Sameer Kumar Jasra; Gianluca Valentino; Alan Muscat; Robert Camilleri
abstract: This paper provides a comparative study of unsupervised machine learning (ML) methods for anomaly detection in flight data monitoring (FDM). The study applies various unsupervised ML techniques to real-world flight data and compares the results to the current state-of-the-art flight data analysis techniques applied in industry. The results are validated by the industrial experts. The study finds that a hybrid Local Outlier Factor (LOF) approach provides significant advantages compared to the current state of the art and other ML techniques because it requires less hyperparameter tuning, reduces the number of false positives, provides an ability to establish trends amongst the entire fleet and has an ability to investigate anomalies at each timestep within every flight. Finally, the study provides an in-depth review for some of the cases highlighted by the hybrid LOF and discusses the particular cases providing insights from an academic and flight safety/operational point of view. The analysis conducted by the human expert regarding the outcomes produced by an ML technique is predominantly absent in scholarly research, thereby offering extra value. The study presents a compelling argument for transitioning from the current approach, based on analyzing occurrences through the exceedances of a threshold value, towards an ML-based method which provides a proactive nature of data analysis. The study shows that there is an untapped opportunity to process flight data and achieve valuable information for enhancing air transport safety and improved aviation operations.

title: INVESTIGATION OF THE NEED TO ADJUST THE ROADS DESIGN STANDARDS OF IN QUARRIES
authors: I. Loginova; O. Kruzhilko; Dmytro Vinivitin
abstract: The purpose of this work is to justify the need to adjust the standards for designing roads in quarries, taking into account the Rules of labour protection in the development of minerals in an open way. The study is based on domestic (experience in Poltava GOK, Yeristovsky GOK) and foreign (mining enterprises in Australia, USA, Canada) practical experience in operating heavy-duty mining vehicles, as well as on a systematic analysis of current norms for technological design of roads in quarries. An analysis of the regulatory and legal issues related to the safety of operation of heavy-duty mining vehicles showed that the Ukrainian standards for designing roads in opencast mines have not changed 25 years. At the same time, the fleet of technological dump trucks used in quarries, technical characteristics, capabilities and prospects for their use, have significantly changed. The study and identification of the advantages of using roads with a constant slope without the installation of horizontal platforms provides the basis for developing recommendations for updating the design standards for roads in open pits, as the current standards do not meet the requirements for the safe operation of modern heavy-duty mining vehicles. It is proposed to update regulatory legal acts by reviewing them with corrective amendments, taking into account the appropriate level of safety when using heavy trucks. Implementation of the proposed standards to improve the transport scheme of the quarry will contribute to the safe operation of heavy mining vehicles.

title: Architecting Self-Governing AI Systems: Field Applications of Decentralized Intelligence in Autonomous Digital Operations
authors: Shreyas Subhash Sawant
venue: International Journal of Computing and Engineering
abstract: The proliferation of autonomous systems across critical infrastructure, supply chains, and digital services has revealed fundamental constraints in centralized AI architectures, where traditional command-and-control frameworks struggle with dynamic complexity and scale demands of modern digital ecosystems. Self-Governing AI Systems (SGAS) emerge as a paradigmatic shift toward distributed intelligence, enabling autonomous agents to collectively manage digital operations through emergent coordination rather than centralized orchestration. This architectural innovation draws inspiration from biological systems, distributed computing principles, and game-theoretic frameworks to create resilient, adaptive, and scalable AI infrastructures. The SGAS framework encompasses three foundational pillars: autonomous decision nodes that combine local sensory capabilities with contextual reasoning, distributed consensus mechanisms that ensure system coherence without centralized control, and adaptive coordination protocols that facilitate dynamic collaboration through negotiation-based resource allocation. Implementation methodologies address communication architectures, decision-making algorithms, and integration strategies through layered approaches that separate concerns while maintaining system coherence. Field validation across real-time infrastructure orchestration, autonomous compliance enforcement, and multi-agent logistics routing demonstrates superior performance characteristics compared to centralized alternatives. The distributed architecture eliminates communication bottlenecks, enables immediate decision-making based on local information, and provides enhanced fault tolerance where individual node failures do not compromise overall system functionality. Performance evaluation reveals consistent improvements in decision-making speed, robustness to system failures, near-linear scalability, and substantial resource utilization efficiency gains.

title: Adaptive Criticality-Based Maintenance (ABC): A Dynamic Strategy Fit-For-Remaining Life Offshore Platform
authors: S. Thamsangakul; P. Srisuppalak; K. Sasanas
venue: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
abstract: Abstract Late-life offshore assets face escalating challenges in sustaining reliability under declining production, evolving risk profiles, and increasingly constrained logistics. Traditional time-based maintenance, although effective during peak-production years, frequently drives inefficient resource allocation and unnecessary interventions that are misaligned with an asset's actual value or remaining economic life. This paper presents an Adaptive Criticality-Based Maintenance (ABC) framework applied to more than 200 offshore wellhead platforms (WHPs) in the Gulf of Thailand. The approach dynamically aligns maintenance and inspection strategies with production potential, remaining life, risk exposure, and offshore logistics constraints across multiple asset types of production, hub, and water injection facilities and a broad equipment population spanning mechanical systems, cranes, booster compressors, electrical and instrumentation (E&I) systems, pressure vessel, piping and safety-critical equipment (SCE). The ABC framework integrates production forecasting, risk-based analysis, and equipment criticality into a unified decision model. Platforms are categorized using Field Development Plan (FDP) data into three tiers "No" production ( P2 MMSCFD) providing a value-based basis for prioritization. Criticality is assessed on safety impact, production consequence, and failure likelihood, consistent with As Low as Reasonably Practicable (ALARP) principles, and strategies are optimized through a blend of preventive maintenance (PM), condition-based maintenance (CBM), and risk-based inspection (RBI). Implementation proceeded through cross-functional workshops, structured stakeholder engagement, and integration into the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), establishing a closed-loop link between planning, risk assessment, and execution. The portfolio was classified into high-production (14%), low-production (51%), and no-production (11%) WHPs, enabling differentiated strategies. The optimization reduced logistics demand including a decrease in the active crew-boat vessel fleet 10% while lowering maintenance workload and offshore personnel exposure through the elimination of low-value activities. CBM principles were extended to crane and booster compressor components alongside continued inspection optimization. By mid of 2026, the year end 2026 forecast compares with the 2025 baseline show 13% reduction in Maintenance and Inspection (M&I) cost per platform across the combined preventive, corrective, and modification workload. Collectively, these results demonstrate improved resource efficiency, operational flexibility, and cost-effectiveness while preserving asset integrity, offering a scalable and replicable model for "fit-for-remaining-life" management of mature offshore assets.

abstract: The aim of this work is to design a fuel supply installation for a fleet of trucks dedicated to the transport of banana bunches from the production sites to the packaging facilities for their future export. The installation will be integrated within an agricultural-industrial environment, ensuring compliance with the necessary technical and regulatory requirements. The project involves the design and calculation of the fuel supply system, considering safety, efficiency, and environmental impact. To achieve this objective, the necessary infrastructure, storage, and distribution systems have been designed. In addition, the required hydraulic and electrical installations have been defined according to the applicable regulations. For its potential execution, a detailed budget has been prepared, along with the necessary technical documentation and plans. Finally, various legal provisions have been applied, and specialized software tools have been used for calculations and design development.
